\label{con:egt-edge-guard-update}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Combine the two edge tests.} Let $P\subseteq W\times E$ be an enabling carrier and let
$G_i\subseteq P\times P$ be specified edge conditions. Put
\[
 T_i=(\pi_W\times\pi_W)^*R_i\cap G_i.
\]
This is another object of $\mathbf{Fr}_N/M$, so Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-action-presentation}
gives an action-model presentation.
  \item \textbf{Recover ordinary product update.} Ordinary product update is the case
$G_i=(\pi_E\times\pi_E)^*S_i$. State-dependent edge conditions
provide a semantic counterpart of arrow updates. The syntactic arrow-update
literature has its own expressivity and synthesis results
\citep{VanDitmarschEtAl2020ArrowUpdateSynthesis};
those results are not being inferred from this set-based presentation.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{construction}[Finite operational realization of action enablement]
\label{con:egt-finite-action-enablement}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Form the enabling strategy.} For finite $W,E$ and an action-enabling predicate
$P\hookrightarrow W\times E$, let $U=\{P\}$, regarded as its finite
set of enabled pairs. Define a strategy
\[
 a_P:D(W)\longrightarrow D(U)
\]
with one negative input event $n_w$ for every $w\in W$ and one
positive event $o_{w,e}$ for every $(w,e)\in U$. Generate the causal
edges $n_w<o_{w,e}$. Different input branches conflict; within a
branch the positive events conflict, so at most one enabled pair is
emitted.
  \item \textbf{Label its events.} Label the negative event by $w$ at the input boundary and
the positive event by $(w,e)$ at the output boundary. Thus the
completed outputs following an input $w$ are exactly the enabled
actions $(w,e)\in U$.
  \item \textbf{Realize the updated observations.} For an updated value term $v^+:U\to Z$,
corestrict to its finite image $F=v^+[U]$ and compose $a_P$ with
$\widehat{\bar v^+}:D(U)\to D(F)$. If updated S5 observations are
supplied, their finite image quotients likewise have the response
strategies of Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-functions}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{proposition}[Sound operational realization of finite action models]
\label{prop:egt-finite-action-enablement}
The map $a_P$ is a receptive courteous strategy. Its enabled output
relation is precisely $P$ and its composition with any finite-image
updated observable returns that observable on each completed updated
pair. Hence every finite semantic action-model enabling relation and
its specified finite-image postconditions admit explicit concurrent
operational realizations, while the action uncertainty relations
$S_i$ remain ordinary epistemic data until observation protocols are
specified. Countable action presentations admit the same carrier-based
construction; uncountable $\mathbf{Set}$-based action models belong to
the ordinary dependent semantics and are not claimed to be single
countable operational arenas.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Causal execution.} The source has finite principal pasts. Its consistency relation is
hereditary and closed under adjoining causes, so it is an event
structure. Every source configuration maps injectively to a
configuration of $D(W)^\perp\parallel D(U)$.
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At the empty source
configuration every negative input $w$ has exactly the lift $n_w$;
after one input all other negative inputs conflict in the arena. All new immediate causal edges are negative-to-positive. Thus the
map is receptive and courteous.
  \item \textbf{Causal execution.} Every source configuration containing
an output has $n_w$ and precisely one event $o_{w,e}$, with $P(w,e)$;
conversely, each
$(w,e)\in P$ exhibits such a configuration. If no action is enabled at
$w$, the maximal source configuration $\{n_w\}$ has no positive
output.
  \item \textbf{Composition.} Composing with the response strategy for the
corestriction of $v^+$ gives the value $v^+(w,e)$ by
Equation~\eqref{eq:egt-value-state-naturality} and composition of
finite response strategies. The same proof uses countably many
branches and outputs when the carriers are countable; every
individual causal past remains finite.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


\begin{proposition}[Knowledge reduction for epistemic actions]
\label{prop:egt-action-knowledge-reduction}
Put $K_i=[R_i]$ on $W$ and $K_i^{\mathcal E}=[R_i^{\mathcal E}]$
on $U$. For every $Q\hookrightarrow U$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:egt-action-knowledge-reduction}
 [\mathcal E,e]K_i^{\mathcal E}Q
 =P_e\Rightarrow
   \bigwedge_{f:\,S_i(e,f)}K_i([\mathcal E,f]Q).
\end{equation}
The empty meet is $\top$. Ordinary conjunction and unchanged atomic
predicates have the reductions
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 [\mathcal E,e](Q\wedge Q')
   &=[\mathcal E,e]Q\wedge[\mathcal E,e]Q',\\
 [\mathcal E,e]p^*V&=P_e\Rightarrow V.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The same predicate doctrine interprets belief modalities for arbitrary
$R_i$, without asserting factivity.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At a state $w\in P_e$, the left side requires $Q(w',f)$ for every
$(w',f)\in U$ satisfying $wR_iw'$ and $eS_if$. Reordering the
quantifiers yields
\[
 \forall f\;(eS_if\Rightarrow
   \forall w'\;(wR_iw'\Rightarrow(P_f(w')\Rightarrow Q(w',f)))).
\]
The inner assertion is $K_i([\mathcal E,f]Q)(w)$. At states outside
$P_e$ both sides are true. Preservation of meets by the right adjoint
and $a_e^*p^*V=a_e^*V$ prove the other equations.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Observation quotients after action update]
\label{prop:egt-action-observation-quotient}
If $R_i=\ker(o_i)$ and $S_i=\ker(b_i)$ for maps
$o_i:W\to O_i$ and $b_i:E\to L_i$, then
\[
 R_i^{\mathcal E}
 =\ker\bigl(\langle o_ip,b_iq\rangle:U\to O_i\times L_i\bigr).
\]
Its image factorization is the effective updated observation quotient.
In particular S5 knowledge, the invariant-predicate adjunctions, and
the common-knowledge quotient construction remain available after the
update, including when $U$ is empty.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Descent along the kernel pair.} Two updated pairs have the same displayed observation exactly when
their old observations and action observations agree. This is the
conjunction of their two kernel-pair relations, which is
Equation~\eqref{eq:egt-action-updated-relation}. Image factorization
and Corollary~\ref{prop:egt-observation-interior} give the effective
quotient.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} Equivalence relations and their generated common-knowledge
relation restrict to the new carrier as constructed, with the empty
case interpreted in the ordinary predicate doctrine.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[Private epistemic information cannot be reduced to announcement]
Let $W=\{w_0,w_1\}$, let two owners initially have the indiscrete
observation equivalence, and take $E=\{e_0,e_1\}$ with
$P_{e_k}=\{w_k\}$. Give owner $1$ the diagonal action relation and
owner $2$ the indiscrete action relation. Then
$U=\{(w_0,e_0),(w_1,e_1)\}$. Owner $1$'s updated relation is equality,
while owner $2$'s still relates both points. Neither original state is
removed. Hence this is a genuine private-information update, not the
public restriction of a subset of $W$.
\end{example}

\begin{construction}[Sequential semantic action update]
\label{con:egt-action-sequential}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Specify the two stages.} Let $\mathcal E=(E,(S_i),P)$ update a relation model on $W$ to
$U=\{P\}$. Let $\mathcal F=(F,(T_i),Q)$ be an action model over
$U$, with $Q\hookrightarrow U\times F$.
  \item \textbf{Construct the composite update.} Define the composite
$\mathcal E\diamond\mathcal F$ over $W$ with action set $E\times F$,
action relations $S_i\boxtimes T_i$, and enabling predicate
\begin{equation}\label{eq:egt-action-composite-precondition}
 P\diamond Q\,(w,e,f)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 P(w,e)\wedge Q((w,e),f).
\end{equation}
The expression involving $Q$ is evaluated only in the fibre where
$P(w,e)$ holds, equivalently by the image under comprehension of the
second enabling object. Updated value terms on the two-stage carrier
are transported by the same canonical reassociation.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[Coherent composition of epistemic actions]
\label{thm:egt-action-composition}
There is a canonical isomorphism of relation models and their retained
updated ordinary terms
\begin{equation}\label{eq:egt-action-composition}
 (W\odot\mathcal E)\odot\mathcal F
 \cong W\odot(\mathcal E\diamond\mathcal F),
 \qquad ((w,e),f)\longmapsto(w,(e,f)).
\end{equation}
It satisfies associativity and the singleton everywhere-enabled unit
laws, including coherent substitution in the reference state. The
corresponding dynamic modalities satisfy
\[
 [\mathcal E,e][\mathcal F,f]Q
   =[\mathcal E\diamond\mathcal F,(e,f)]Q
\]
under the indicated identification of final predicates.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Predicate calculation.} The two carriers are defined by the identical conjunction of the two
enablement tests after reassociation. The two-stage relation between
$((w,e),f)$ and $((w',e'),f')$ is
\[
 R_i(w,w')\wedge S_i(e,e')\wedge T_i(f,f'),
\]
which is the relation of the combined action model. Updated terms are
the same functions on these identified points.
  \item \textbf{Adjunction and transposition.} Reassociation of
triples and quadruples obeys Cartesian coherence, including the unit
comparison. For the dynamic box, two successive right adjoints along
the inclusions of the action components agree with the right adjoint
along their composite by uniqueness of right adjoints; the elementwise
precondition is Equation~\eqref{eq:egt-action-composite-precondition}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent Two consecutive epistemic action updates associate by matching the intermediate state.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
(W\odot\mathcal E)\odot\mathcal F\arrow[r,"\cong"]\arrow[d,"p_1"']
 &W\odot(\mathcal E\diamond\mathcal F)\arrow[d,"p"]\\
 W\odot\mathcal E\arrow[r,"p"']&W
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{remark}[Scope of epistemic action models]
\label{rem:egt-action-scope}
The construction is fully semantic: $P$, $R_i$, $S_i$, and updated
observable terms are ordinary typed data. Syntactic precondition or
postcondition languages are not required. The update changes the
state carrier as well as both endpoints of each accessibility relation;
it is not the reference pullback of
Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-reference-bc}. A state map that forgets
accessible alternatives need not preserve knowledge formulas merely
because it preserves the underlying updated carrier. The bounded
morphism and alternative-lifting results of
Section~\ref{sec:egt-modal-transport} address that distinction.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Action models transport across bounded state quotients]
\label{cor:egt-action-bounded-quotient}
Let $f:X\twoheadrightarrow Y$ be a surjective bounded morphism from
relations $R_i$ to $\bar R_i$. Give $Y$ an epistemic action model with
action set $E$, action relations $S_i$, and enabling subobject
$\bar P\hookrightarrow Y\times E$. Pull it back along $f\times1_E$
to form the action model over $X$. The induced map on updated carriers
\[
 f^+:X\odot\mathcal E\longrightarrow Y\odot\bar{\mathcal E},
 \qquad(x,e)\longmapsto(f(x),e)
\]
is a surjective bounded morphism for the updated relations. For every
$e\in E$ and $\bar Q\hookrightarrow Y\odot\bar{\mathcal E}$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 f^*[\bar{\mathcal E},e]\bar Q
   &=[\mathcal E,e](f^+)^*\bar Q,\\
 f^*\langle\bar{\mathcal E},e\rangle\bar Q
   &=\langle\mathcal E,e\rangle(f^+)^*\bar Q.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Hence it preserves and reflects every modal fixed-point assertion with
atomic tests descended through $f^+$, including updated knowledge
assertions and their dynamic action tests.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Lifting along the surjection.} For an enabled $(y,e)$, surjectivity of $f$ supplies $x$ with $f(x)=y$;
the pullback enabling predicate makes $(x,e)$ enabled. Thus $f^+$ is
surjective. Forward preservation of accessibility is inherited from
$f$, with the unchanged action relation $S_i$.
  \item \textbf{Construction of the comparison.} Given a reduced
updated alternative $(y',e')$ accessible from $(f(x),e)$, the back
clause of $f$ supplies $x'$ with $xR_ix'$ and $f(x')=y'$. Since
$\bar P(y',e')$, its pullback $P(x',e')$ holds. Thus $(x',e')$ is the
required updated alternative.
  \item \textbf{Base-change comparison.} The action-component comprehensions
of the two models form pullback squares along $f$; both
Beck--Chevalley identities of Theorem~\ref{thm:fib-comprehension}
give the dynamic box and diamond equations. Apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-modal-adequacy} to $f^+$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Lifting alternatives and preserving fixed points}
\label{sec:egt-modal-transport}

A map between epistemic models may preserve actual states and
forward accessibility while still losing alternatives quantified over
by a modality. Exact modal transport therefore needs two comparisons:
every concrete successor has an abstract image, and every abstract
successor at an image state lifts to a concrete successor at the same
reference. These are the forward and back conditions of a bounded
morphism. With both, the modal and fixed-point predicates descend
without deleting relevant alternatives.

\begin{definition}[Bounded morphism]
\label{def:egt-bounded-morphism}
A map $q:X\to Y$ between families of relation frames is \textbf{bounded} if,
for every relation index $a$,
\[
 xR_ax'\Longrightarrow q(x)\bar R_aq(x'),
\]
and every $q(x)\bar R_ay'$ has a lift $xR_ax'$ with $q(x')=y'$.
For interpreted atomic predicates require $P_X=q^*P_Y$.
The second clause is equivalently fibrewise coverage by the canonical comparison to the cartesian lift,
\[
 R_a\longrightarrow X\times_{Y,\bar p_1}\bar R_a,
 \qquad(x,x')\longmapsto(x,(q(x),q(x'))).
\]
\end{definition}

\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
 R_a\arrow[r,two heads]\arrow[dr,"p_1"']&
 X\times_Y\bar R_a\arrow[d]\arrow[r]&\bar R_a\arrow[d,"\bar p_1"]\\
 &X\arrow[r,"q"']&Y
\end{tikzcd}
\]

\begin{theorem}[Modal fixed-point adequacy]
\label{thm:egt-modal-adequacy}
Let $q:X\to Y$ be a bounded morphism. Interpret every free predicate
variable by a valuation $\rho$ on $Y$ and by its componentwise pullback
$q^*\rho$ on $X$; interpret each designated atomic predicate on $X$ as
the pullback of its interpretation on $Y$. Then every formula of the
positive modal fixed-point language satisfies the naturality equation
\[
 \llbracket\varphi\rrbracket_X(q^*\rho)
 =q^*\llbracket\varphi\rrbracket_Y(\rho).
\]
This includes nested least and greatest fixed points. Validity is
preserved; if $q$ is surjective it is also reflected.
\end{theorem}

\noindent Forward preservation of accessibility is a commuting square on relation witnesses.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
R_i\arrow[r,"f\times f"]\arrow[d,hook]
 &S_i\arrow[d,hook]\\
 X\times X\arrow[r,"f\times f"']
 &Y\times Y
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}


\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Construction of the comparison.} Fix the valuation $\rho$ on the target and its pulled-back valuation
$q^*\rho$ on the source. Induct on formulas in the assertion fibres. The variable and atomic cases follow from these interpretations by
definition.
  \item \textbf{Lifting through the comparison.} Reindexing preserves the remaining logical operations by
Theorem~\ref{thm:fib-comprehension}. The comparison to the cartesian
alternative context has the displayed fibrewise lifts; quantifying those
fibres gives
$[R_a]q^*=q^*[\bar R_a]$ and
$\langle R_a\rangle q^*=q^*\langle\bar R_a\rangle$ by respectively
universal and existential quantification over the corresponding fibers.
  \item \textbf{Fixed-point argument.} For a fixed-point body the induction hypothesis gives
$F_Xq^*=q^*F_Y$. Since $q^*\mu F_Y$ is fixed,
$\mu F_X\leq q^*\mu F_Y$. Put $Q=\forall_q\mu F_X$.
  \item \textbf{Adjunction and transposition.} Then $q^*Q\leq\mu F_X$, whence
$q^*F_YQ=F_Xq^*Q\leq\mu F_X$. Adjunction gives $F_YQ\leq Q$;
leastness and the counit give
$q^*\mu F_Y\leq q^*Q\leq\mu F_X$. For greatest fixed points put $Q=\exists_q\nu F_X$.
  \item \textbf{Unit and identity laws.} The unit gives $\nu F_X\leq q^*Q$, hence
$\nu F_X=F_X\nu F_X\leq q^*F_YQ$. Adjunction gives $Q\leq F_YQ$, and coinduction gives
$\nu F_X\leq q^*Q\leq q^*\nu F_Y$. The reverse inequality holds because $q^*\nu F_Y$ is fixed.
  \item \textbf{Fixed-point argument.} For nested fixed points, first apply structural induction to the body
with a designated free variable $p$: for every target candidate
$U\in\mathsf{Pred}(Y)$ its source instance uses $q^*U$, giving
$F_X(q^*U)=q^*F_Y(U)$ with all other free variables interpreted by
$q^*\rho$. The two adjunction arguments above then establish the
fixed-point comparison for the binder of $p$.
  \item \textbf{Descent along the kernel pair.} Inducting on binding depth
proves the displayed equation for nested least and greatest fixed
points, without treating arbitrary source valuations as descending. Finally, a surjective $q$ reflects the top predicate.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


\subsubsection{Local retained witnesses and exact modal transport}
\label{sec:sheaf-retained-modal}

A secured history can retain events that are not visible at the chosen
observation boundary.  Localizing that history and forgetting evidence
are different operations: an internal epistemic test after restricting
away a receipt can be more demanding than the completed-state test.
We therefore localize on patches that keep the specified observed
receptions and institutional certificate occurrences.  This uses the
actual delivered-record extraction of
Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data}, not a new event
observation stipulated independently of the protocol.  The distinction
is related to the sheaf treatment of epistemic update in
\citet{Kishida2013}.

\begin{construction}[Observation anchor and retained-state image]
\label{con:sheaf-anchored-observation}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Construct the least observation anchor.} Work in
the policy-indexed secured-witness family $\mathscr K_X$ of
Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-owned-witness-family} over $E$.
Let $H\subseteq|E|$ be the union of the exhibited matched recipient
occurrences, issuer and certificate occurrences, and, for a
completed boundary, the public final-report occurrences.  These
are read from the specified protocol wires.  For $U\subseteq|E|$
define the monotone operation
\begin{align*}
 \Phi_H(U)={}&H\cup\downarrow_EU\\
 &{}\cup\bigcup_{x\in X}f_x
        [\downarrow_{S_x}f_x^{-1}(U)]
 \cup\bigcup_{x\in X}g_x
        [\downarrow_{T_x}g_x^{-1}(U)].
\end{align*}
Put $U_0=\varnothing$, $U_{n+1}=\Phi_H(U_n)$ and
\[
 A=\bigcup_{n<\omega}U_n.
\]
Inverse images, direct images and down-closure commute with
unions of increasing chains; hence $\Phi_H(A)=A$.  This fixed-point
equation is precisely simultaneous saturation and inclusion of $H$.
Every saturated patch containing $H$ contains each $U_n$ by
induction, so contains $A$.  Therefore $A$ is the least such patch;
for the finite protocol the iteration stabilizes in finitely many
steps.  Equivalently, this closure is left adjoint to the inclusion
of saturated patches in $\mathcal P(|E|)$.
  \item \textbf{Form the anchored site.} Put
\[
 \mathcal O_A=\{U\in\mathcal O_X:A\subseteq U\}
\]
with the covering families inherited from $\mathcal O_X$; every
intersection of two anchored patches still contains $A$.  Write
$\mathscr K_A$ for the restricted sheaf.  The state at a patch $U$
retains the entire matching graph over $U$, and its restriction to
$A$ is independent of the choice of anchored patch.
  \item \textbf{Read exactly the retained data.} Let
$\operatorname{rec}_{i,A}$ extract from the matched causal history
on $A$ the received labelled subhistory specified by the finite
communication protocol.  It keeps the distinguished recipient
occurrences and the delivered values, not merely the set of interface
labels.  Retain also the actual public final-output subhistory
$\operatorname{rec}_{0,A}$; when there is no public output its
record carrier is $1$.  Let $\operatorname{cert}_A$ retain the
specified issuer-produced certificate occurrences and their matched
provenance.  Form the tuple
\[
 d_A:\mathscr K_X(A)\longrightarrow D,
 \qquad d_A(x,\varphi)
 =\bigl(x,\operatorname{rec}_{0,A}(x,\varphi),
       (\operatorname{rec}_{i,A}(x,\varphi))_i,
       \operatorname{cert}_A(x,\varphi)\bigr),
\]
where the codomain is formed in the existing ordinary slice over
$X$.  Explicitly, let $V_{0,x},V_{i,x},C_x$ be the images of the
indicated public, recipient, and issuer-port restriction functions
on the finite labelled histories over $x$ (use $1$ for an absent
port).  These restriction functions read the designated event
occurrences, their labels and induced secured causal orders, together
with any displayed local register projected from $x$.  Their images
are sets, constructed by the ordinary image factorization.  Put
\[
 D=D_X=\coprod_{x\in X}
      \bigl(V_{0,x}\times\prod_iV_{i,x}\times C_x\bigr).
\]
The displayed $x$ in $d_A(x,\varphi)$ denotes the coproduct tag.
For the finite implementation the image inclusions into the already
constructed global record carriers identify this readout with the
public and recipient maps $d_0,d_i:\Xi\to V_0,V_i$ of
Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data}, by the explicit
comparison in Proposition~\ref{prop:sheaf-finite-port-readout}.
Thus no extra observation map or uniformity axiom is introduced.
  \item \textbf{Construct the image quotient.} Put
$T=\operatorname{im}(d_A)$ and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-retained-quotient}
 q_U:\mathscr K_A(U)\longrightarrow T,
 \qquad q_U(k)=d_A(k|_A),
\end{equation}
using the corestriction of $d_A$ to its image.  These functions
commute with restriction and hence determine
$q:\mathscr K_A\to\underline T$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{lemma}[Local extension and objectwise surjectivity]
\label{lem:sheaf-retained-surjection}
For every anchored patch $U$, a local matching $(x,\varphi)$
can be regarded as the same secured matching on the full interface;
this gives a map $j_U:\mathscr K_A(U)\to\mathscr K_A(E)$ with
$\operatorname{res}_{E,U}j_U=\id$.  The retained quotient
$q_U:\mathscr K_A(U)\twoheadrightarrow T$ is surjective for every
$U$.  Thus $q$ is a regular epimorphism of sheaves.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Extend the matching graph.} Since $U$ is saturated,
configurations of the restricted source structures are also global
configurations, and their matched graph has the same secured causal
order.  Regard the graph as a global matching without inserting any
new event.  Restriction returns the original graph.
  \item \textbf{Lift every retained record.} Every $t\in T$ has a
preimage $k_A\in\mathscr K_X(A)$ by definition of the image.
Extend $k_A$ to the full interface with $j_A$ and restrict that
global matching to $U$.  Its restriction back to $A$ equals $k_A$,
so its image under $q_U$ is $t$.  This constructs a lift at every
patch.  A sectionwise surjective sheaf morphism is an epimorphism,
and every epimorphism in a Grothendieck topos is regular.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent The retained quotient is read from an anchored causal
history, not from an arbitrary hidden scalar.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathscr K_A(U)\arrow[r,"(-)|_A"]\arrow[dr,"q_U"']&
 \mathscr K_X(A)\arrow[d,"d_A"]\\
 &T\arrow[r,hook]&D
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{construction}[Lifted epistemic and strategic relations]
\label{con:sheaf-lifted-relations}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Distinguish receipts from updated knowledge.} The
record quotient $T$ has a constructed recipient-record projection
$r_i:T\to V_i$, and $\kerpair(r_i)$ tests equality of delivered
receipts.  It is not, in general, the owner's updated epistemic
relation: the latter also retains the original world observation.
For completed situated protocols, the canonical surjection
$v_W:T_W\twoheadrightarrow U_W$ and the observation
$\beta_i=o_i^+v_W$ are constructed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-updated-action-comparison}.  The updated
relation on $T_W$ is $R_i^{T_W}=\kerpair(\beta_i)$; distributed
knowledge uses $\bigcap_{i\in C}R_i^{T_W}$ and common knowledge
the reflexive transitive closure of their union.  Their definitions
are thus pulled back from actual delivered action events.
  \item \textbf{Retain owner-coordinate deviations.} The first
component of $T$ includes $x$ and its complete policy $p(x)$.
After selecting a situated reference-world projection $w:T\to W$
(or pulling back the finite-input carrier along the given state map),
for a coalition $C$ put
\[
 tD_C^Tt'\iff w(t)=w(t')\ \wedge\
                  p_{-C}(t)=p_{-C}(t').
\]
On a legal (or completed legal) retained subcarrier replace this
relation by its restriction to that carrier.  This relation lies above the original owner-coordinate deviation
span.  Its different execution records are alternative \emph{witnesses},
not additional choices controlled by the owner; improving comparisons
on those records require the manuscript's explicit witness quantifiers
or descent to policy values.
  \item \textbf{Pull back the relation.} For any such relation
$R\hookrightarrow T\times T$, define the relation sheaf
\[
 \mathscr R=(q\times q)^*\underline R
 \rightrightarrows\mathscr K_A.
\]
Its source and target are the projections of the kernel-style
pullback, not event-structure polarities.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[Sourcewise lifting and exact modal descent]
\label{thm:sheaf-modal-descent}
For every retained relation $R\hookrightarrow T^2$ constructed in
Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-lifted-relations}, including the
world-indexed relations of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-updated-action-comparison}, the comparison over
$\mathscr K_A$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-sourcewise-lift}
 \lambda_R:\mathscr R\longrightarrow
 \mathscr K_A\times_{\underline T,p_1}\underline R,
 \quad (k,k')\longmapsto(k,(qk,qk'))
\end{equation}
is a regular epimorphism.  For every predicate $P\hookrightarrow T$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-modal-preservation}
 q^*[R]P=[\mathscr R]q^*P,
 \qquad
 q^*\langle R\rangle P=\langle\mathscr R\rangle q^*P.
\end{equation}
The same equalities hold for distributed knowledge and common knowledge
formed from the indicated relations, with the common-knowledge operator
interpreted by its finite-path accessibility relation.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Identify the source-fixed pullback.} The comparison
$\lambda_R$ is canonically the base change of
$q:\mathscr K_A\twoheadrightarrow\underline T$ along
$\underline R\xrightarrow{p_2}\underline T$:
\[
 \mathscr R\cong
 (\mathscr K_A\times_{\underline T,p_1}\underline R)
 \times_{\underline T,p_2}\mathscr K_A.
\]
Thus $\lambda_R$ is a regular epimorphism by pullback stability.
Concretely, for each prescribed source $k$ and retained successor
$(qk,t')\in R$, the regular-epi fibre supplies a target witness
above $t'$ without changing $k$.
  \item \textbf{Apply quantifier base change.} Factor the source
projection of $\mathscr R$ through $\lambda_R$ and the cartesian
source pullback.  For a regular epimorphism $e$, its inverse image
on subobjects is order-reflecting and
$\exists_e e^*Q=Q=\forall_e e^*Q$.
Applying these equalities to $\lambda_R$ and then Beck--Chevalley to
the source pullback proves both equations in
\eqref{eq:sheaf-modal-preservation}.  These are standard regular-topos
calculations \citep[Chapters~IV--V]{MacLaneMoerdijk1992Sheaves};
no independently stipulated modal lift is used.
  \item \textbf{Preserve collective modalities.} The distributed
knowledge relation is the displayed intersection of observation
kernel pairs; the same calculation applies to that single relation.
For common knowledge, lift each edge of a finite retained $C$-path
from its given source using the first step.  Conversely every lifted
path projects to a retained path.  Hence the finite-path relation
has exactly the same source-fixed alternatives, and its box is
preserved.  Inverse image preserves the Boolean operations on
predicates pulled back from the constant retained carrier; regular
epicity reflects equality of those predicates.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Ordinary-predicate adjoints for the retained quotient]
\label{lem:sheaf-ordinary-predicate-adjoints}
For the retained-record quotient
$q:\mathscr K_A\twoheadrightarrow\underline T$, define
\[
 H:\mathcal P(T)\longrightarrow\Sub(\mathscr K_A),\qquad
 H(P)(U)=\{k\in\mathscr K_A(U):q_U(k)\in P\}.
\]
For $B\hookrightarrow\mathscr K_A$, put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-ordinary-predicate-adjoints}
 \begin{aligned}
 H_!(B)&=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal O_A}q_U[B(U)],\\
 H_*(B)&=\{t\in T:\forall U\in\mathcal O_A\ \forall k\in\mathscr K_A(U),
                    \ q_U(k)=t\Rightarrow k\in B(U)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Then $H_!\dashv H\dashv H_*$. The map $H$ preserves all meets,
all joins and complements of ordinary predicates, and reflects order.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Construct the ordinary-predicate comparison.}
Constant presheaves on the retained site are sheaves. Thus $H(P)$
is the pullback of $\underline P\hookrightarrow\underline T$ along
$q$, and is a subobject of $\mathscr K_A$. The patch category is
small, so the displayed union and universal quantification define
ordinary subsets of $T$.
  \item \textbf{Verify both adjunctions.} For $P\subseteq T$,
\[
 H_!(B)\subseteq P
 \iff\forall U\ B(U)\subseteq q_U^{-1}(P)
 \iff B\leq H(P),
\]
and
\[
 P\subseteq H_*(B)
 \iff\forall U\ q_U^{-1}(P)\subseteq B(U)
 \iff H(P)\leq B.
\]
These prove $H_!\dashv H\dashv H_*$, so $H$ preserves all
meets and joins in the indicated lattices.
  \item \textbf{Preserve complements and reflect order.} The
subobjects $H(P)$ and $H(T\setminus P)$ have empty intersection
and union $\mathscr K_A$, so they are complementary. If
$H(P)\leq H(Q)$ and $t\in P$, the sectionwise surjectivity
constructed in Lemma~\ref{lem:sheaf-retained-surjection} supplies
a lift of $t$ at a patch. That lift lies in $H(Q)$, hence $t\in Q$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

The internal adjoints along $q$ have codomain $\Sub(\underline T)$
\citep[Chapters~IV--V]{MacLaneMoerdijk1992Sheaves}. The displayed
$H_!,H_*$ instead have codomain $\mathcal P(T)$, which is the
ordinary predicate lattice used by the retained modal model.


\begin{corollary}[Retained fixed-point modal transport]
\label{cor:sheaf-modal-fixed-point}
For the same regular epimorphism $q$ and its pulled-back designated
relations, interpret each atomic predicate and each free predicate
variable on $\mathscr K_A$ by pullback from $T$.  Every formula of
the positive Boolean modal fixed-point language, including nested
least and greatest fixed points, satisfies
\[
 \sem{\varphi}_{\mathscr K_A}(q^*\rho)
   =q^*\sem{\varphi}_T(\rho).
\]
Since $q^*$ is order-reflecting, the corresponding retained-image
validity predicates are also reflected.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Compare the ordinary and sheaf predicates.} Use
$H$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:sheaf-ordinary-predicate-adjoints}; on
ordinary predicates it is the $q^*$ in the statement. Atoms and
free variables satisfy the comparison by their interpretation.
The same lemma preserves Boolean operations on these predicates.
  \item \textbf{Transport modal alternatives.} The relation sheaf
is $(q\times q)^*\underline R$. Its source-fixed comparison is a
regular epimorphism by Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-modal-descent},
which gives the box and diamond equations on ordinary predicates.
These are the forward and lifting comparisons of
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-modal-adequacy}, including the universal tests
after further causal restriction.
  \item \textbf{Transport the least fixed point.} For a positive
body write $F$ for its operator on $\mathcal P(T)$ and
$\widehat F$ for its operator on $\Sub(\mathscr K_A)$.
Induction on the body gives $\widehat F H=HF$. Put
$m=\mu\widehat F$. Since $H(\mu F)$ is fixed,
$m\leq H(\mu F)$. For $Q=H_*m$, the counit gives
$HQ\leq m$, hence
\[
 H(FQ)=\widehat F(HQ)\leq\widehat F(m)=m.
\]
By adjunction, $FQ\leq H_*m=Q$. Therefore
$\mu F\leq Q$ and $H(\mu F)\leq HQ\leq m$, proving
$H(\mu F)=\mu\widehat F$.
  \item \textbf{Transport the greatest fixed point.} Put
$n=\nu\widehat F$. The fixed point $H(\nu F)$ satisfies
$H(\nu F)\leq n$. For $Q=H_!n$, the unit gives $n\leq HQ$,
so
\[
 n=\widehat F(n)\leq\widehat F(HQ)=H(FQ).
\]
Adjunction gives $Q=H_!n\leq FQ$. Thus $Q\leq\nu F$ and
$n\leq HQ\leq H(\nu F)$, establishing
$H(\nu F)=\nu\widehat F$.
  \item \textbf{Iterate through binders and reflect validity.}
Apply these two calculations inductively at each binder. The remaining
free-variable valuation is always transported by $H$. Order
reflection in Lemma~\ref{lem:sheaf-ordinary-predicate-adjoints}
then reflects the retained-image validity predicates.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent The fixed-point comparison uses the ordinary powerset on
the retained side and the full subobject lattice on the witness side.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathcal P(T)\arrow[r,"H"]\arrow[d,"F"']
 &\Sub(\mathscr K_A)\arrow[d,"\widehat F"]\\
 \mathcal P(T)\arrow[r,"H"']&\Sub(\mathscr K_A)
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\noindent The source-fixed witness comparison is a cartesian
base change of the retained-record quotient.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathscr R\arrow[r,"\lambda_R",two heads]\arrow[d]
 &\mathscr K_A\times_{\underline T,p_1}\underline R
     \arrow[d,"p_2"]\\
 \mathscr K_A\arrow[r,"q"',two heads]&\underline T
 \arrow[ul,phantom,"\lrcorner",very near start]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{example}[Forgetting a receipt changes sheaf-internal knowledge]
\label{ex:sheaf-unanchored-knowledge}
Take two reference worlds $w_0,w_1$, indistinguishable before an
exchange.  At $w_0$ one positive receipt event $e$ can occur; at
$w_1$ there is no such event.  At the completed witness $(w_0,\{e\})$
the observed receipt distinguishes $w_0$, so the completed-state test
$K_i(w=w_0)$ holds.  On the unanchored empty causal patch both
witnesses restrict to empty matching graphs and have the same received
event record.  The sheaf-internal universal test considers this
restriction and therefore does not establish $K_i(w=w_0)$.
Anchoring at $e$ eliminates precisely the restriction that erases the
needed evidence.  This demonstrates why the theorem concerns actual
retained observations, not unrestricted sheaf-internal knowledge on
all causal patches.
\end{example}

\begin{remark}[Exact scope of the modal comparison]
The predicates in \eqref{eq:sheaf-modal-preservation} are pulled back
from the retained carrier $T$.  An arbitrary predicate on hidden
matching witnesses need not descend.  If the chosen anchor saturates
to all of $E$, its site has no proper patches: the theorem remains true
but makes no nontrivial new localization claim at that completed
boundary.  Before hiding, the original secured-matching sheaf still
supplies its independent local-to-global reconstruction.  For visible
temporal transitions after hiding, exactness continues to be governed
by the source-fixed successor-lifting comparisons of
Section~\ref{sec:egt-exact-visible-refinement}.
\end{remark}


\subsection{Public announcement in the agent calculus}
\label{agt-sec-public}

\subsubsection{Restricting a situated model}

Let $M$ be a situated model on $W$, and let $\varphi$ be an assertion
interpreted in $M$. Form its comprehension
\[
 j:U=\{w\in W\mid M,w\models\varphi\}\hookrightarrow W.
\]
The updated model $M|\varphi$ is carried by $U$. Its valuations
and linear families are restricted, and observations become $o_i j$,
corestricted to their images when appropriate. Accessibility is
$R_i^U=(j\times j)^*R_i$, so excluded worlds disappear from both
positions of the relation. Strong monoidality of linear restriction
preserves agent types and their composition; only the available
epistemic context changes.

The dynamic type operation is $\Pi_j^\ell$. At a state removed by
the announcement it is the empty additive product $\Top$; at a
retained state it is the post-update fibre. The tensor unit $\I$
cannot be substituted for $\Top$: these are different limits and
resource interpretations.

\begin{theorem}[Perspective after announcement]
\label{agt-thm-announcement-perspective}
For a linear family $A$ over $U$, there is a natural isomorphism
\[
 K_{o j}^\ell A\cong j^*K_o^\ell\Pi_j^\ell A.
\]
It is coherent with successive public restrictions and the monoidal
perspective comparisons.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Adjunction and transposition.} Right adjoints compose: $\Pi_{oj}^\ell\cong\Pi_o^\ell\Pi_j^\ell$. Also $(oj)^*=j^*o^*$. Their composite gives the displayed isomorphism.
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At $u\in U$, the right side takes a product over all old alternatives,
with terminal factors for alternatives outside $U$. Its nonterminal factors
are exactly $A_v$ for $v\in U$ with $o(v)=o(u)$. Product projections prove
the comparison and its coherence. Tensor comparisons on either side are
obtained by tensoring these same remaining projections.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Dynamic formulas and reduction}

The interpretation of a public-announcement formula is
\begin{equation}
 \sem{[!\varphi]\psi}_M
 =\forall_j\sem{\psi}_{M|\varphi}.
 \label{agt-eq-public-semantics}
\end{equation}
The formula $\psi$ is always interpreted in the updated model,
using its restricted accessibility relations. This rule continues to
apply when the postcondition contains knowledge, another announcement,
or a common-knowledge fixed point. Otherwise the reduction would
silently evaluate an epistemic operator against the old alternatives.

\begin{theorem}[Public-announcement reduction laws]
\label{agt-thm-public-reduction}
For an atom $p$ whose valuation is restricted by the update,
\begin{align*}
 [!\varphi]p&\leftrightarrow(\varphi\Rightarrow p),\\
 [!\varphi](\psi\wedge\chi)
 &\leftrightarrow[!\varphi]\psi\wedge[!\varphi]\chi,\\
 [!\varphi]\neg\psi
 &\leftrightarrow\bigl(\varphi\Rightarrow\neg[!\varphi]\psi\bigr),\\
 [!\varphi]K_i\psi
 &\leftrightarrow\bigl(\varphi\Rightarrow K_i([!\varphi]\psi)\bigr),\\
 [!\varphi][!\psi]\chi
 &\leftrightarrow[!(\varphi\wedge[!\varphi]\psi)]\chi.
\end{align*}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At each stage interpret the postformula in the restricted model and
let $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ be the current announcement comprehension. The atomic, Boolean, and knowledge equations follow, respectively,
from inverse image, the monic adjunction identities, and
\eqref{eq:egt-public-update-modal-reduction} of
\cref{thm:egt-public-update-reduction}.
  \item \textbf{Iteration of announcement reduction.} Thus they apply inductively to
postformulas involving knowledge as well as fixed pre-update
predicates. For successive announcements the second comprehension
inside $U$ composes with $j$ to the inclusion classified in $W$ by
$\varphi\wedge[!\varphi]\psi$; the right adjoints of the two
inclusions compose. This gives the final equation and retains the
re-evaluation of epistemic formulas after the first update.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

The reduction equations follow from comprehension and the
right-adjoint interpretation of announcement; compare
\citet{Plaza2007PublicCommunications,BaltagMossSolecki1998PublicAnnouncements}.
They express the logical operation independently of a physical test or
message that might implement it.

\begin{example}[Re-evaluating an epistemic announcement]
Take two indistinguishable worlds, with $p$ true at just one. At that world
$p\wedge\neg K_ip$ is true, so its announcement is enabled. Afterward only
the $p$-world remains and $K_ip$ holds. Thus the announced epistemic formula
itself becomes false. The update recomputes epistemic formulas in the restricted model; the example shows the possible failure of $[!\varphi]\varphi$.
\end{example}

\subsubsection{The effect on policies and resources}

Public restriction can change which observation-based policies are
uniformly legal. For $F\subseteq W\times M$, restricting to $U$
removes some worlds from surviving observation fibres. With
$O_U=\im(oj)$ and $r:O_U\hookrightarrow O$, every former legal
policy restricts to one over the new quotient, giving the map below.
\[
 \Pol_o(F)\longrightarrow\Pol_{oj}((j\times1)^*F),\qquad
 \pi\longmapsto\pi r.
\]
The restriction map need not be injective: policies distinguished
only by observations absent from $U$ become indistinguishable. New
uniformly legal actions may also appear after a counterexample world is
removed. By contrast, linear execution resources are merely reindexed;
a public update does not create a resource or authorization token.

So far the update is logical. To regard it as a physical public
announcement, an enabled test or message must have execution witnesses
whose successful image is exactly $U$. The finite communication protocols
in the next part provide such realizations and make it possible to compare
the epistemic update with the complete policies that produced it.

\begin{proposition}[Observation-based implementability of a public test]
\label{agt-prop-test-implementation}
Let $o:W\twoheadrightarrow O$ be an effective observation and
$P\subseteq W$.  The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item $P$ is the inverse image $o^{-1}(B)$ of a predicate $B\subseteq O$;
\item $P$ is constant on the kernel pair of $o$;
\item its characteristic function factors as $1_P=\chi o$ for
      $\chi:O\to2$.
\end{enumerate}
For finite $O$, these equivalent descriptions give a receptive courteous
protocol accepting the observed input and emitting a success event precisely
at worlds in $P$.  Its successful-execution witness image is the
comprehension $P\hookrightarrow W$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Descent along the kernel pair.} The first and third descriptions are equivalent by taking the
characteristic predicate. Either makes $P$ constant on the kernel pair.
  \item \textbf{Reverse implication.} Conversely kernel-pair constancy lets $1_P$ descend uniquely along the
effective quotient $o$, producing $\chi$ and $B=\chi^{-1}(\{1\})$. For finite $O$, realize $\chi$ by
$\widehat\chi:D(O)\to D(2)$. Connect it to the gate
$D(2)\to D(1)$ whose source accepts both negative bit inputs but
emits its sole positive success output only following input $1$.
  \item \textbf{Lifting through the comparison.} It is receptive because both inputs lift uniquely, and courteous because
its only added dependency is negative-to-positive. The composite emits
success exactly when $\chi(o(w))=1$; the image of successful witnesses
is therefore $P$. The absent success event is not reinterpreted as a
false operational scalar.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} A test of a predicate not constant on the
available observation fibre requires a different actually delivered signal,
not an implicit truth oracle.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\subsection{General epistemic action models and delivery}
\label{agt-sec-actions}

\subsubsection{General action models}

Let an action presentation have event set $E$, event relations $S_i$, and
an enabling predicate $\mathsf{pre}\subseteq W\times E$. Its updated
carrier and relations are
\begin{align}
 U&=\{(w,e):\mathsf{pre}(w,e)\},
 \label{agt-eq-actioncarrier}\\
 (w,e)R_i^+(v,f)&\iff wR_iv\ \wedge\ eS_if.
 \label{agt-eq-actionrelation}
\end{align}
The updated relation is the standard dynamic-epistemic product
update \citep{BaltagMossSolecki1998PublicAnnouncements}. In the
observation-generated case, $R_i=\kerpair(o_i)$ and
$S_i=\kerpair(b_i)$, so the effective updated signal is the image
of $(w,e)\mapsto(o_i(w),b_i(e))$. This construction uses the
information actually delivered by the event.

The projection $r:U\to W$ forgets the event, and $r^*$
transports linear families and agent types across that change of state.
An implemented event also retains a witness family and concurrent
realizer, as in Section~\ref{agt-sec-institutions}. Neither an abstract
event relation nor a semantic update alone supplies an operational
communication wire.

For an event $e$, let $j_e:W_e\hookrightarrow W$ be its enabling inclusion,
and $k_e:W_e\to U$ send $w$ to $(w,e)$. Define
\[
 [\mathcal A,e]\psi=\forall_{j_e}k_e^*\sem\psi_{M\otimes\mathcal A}.
\]
Its type-level version is $\Pi_{j_e}^\ell k_e^*$.

\begin{proposition}[Action reduction and composition]
\label{agt-prop-action}
For a finite event presentation,
\[
 [\mathcal A,e]K_i\psi
 \leftrightarrow
 \mathsf{pre}_e\Rightarrow
 \bigwedge_{f:eS_if}K_i([\mathcal A,f]\psi).
\]
Successive action updates compose by retaining pairs of enabled events,
and this composition is associative up to the canonical tuple bijection.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At an enabled $(w,e)$, knowledge quantifies over exactly the pairs $(v,f)$
with $wR_iv$, $eS_if$, and $\mathsf{pre}(v,f)$. Grouping first by $f$
gives the displayed conjunction and its guarded boxes. At a disabled $w$
both sides are true.
  \item \textbf{Causal execution.} For a second action with precondition $Q$ on $U$,
the sequential carrier consists of triples $(w,e,f)$ with
$\mathsf{pre}(w,e)\wedge Q((w,e),f)$. Its relation is the conjunction
of the original world relation and the two event relations. Reassociating
triples preserves these tests, the reindexed linear families, and, for
implemented actions, the composite concurrent realizer. Fourfold tuple
reassociation proves the coherence diagrams.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Public restriction as singleton action update]
\label{prop:public-singleton-action}
For a state predicate $P\hookrightarrow W$, let the action carrier be
$E=1$, its sole event have enabling predicate $P$, and every action
relation be equality on $1$. Its product update is canonically the
comprehension $j:\{P\}\hookrightarrow W$, with relations
$R_i^+= (j\times j)^*R_i$. The pointed action box and diamond are
$\forall_j$ and $\exists_j$; in particular the corresponding
knowledge-reduction law is
\[
 [!P]K_i\psi\ \longleftrightarrow\
 P\Rightarrow K_i([!P]\psi).
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Monoidal comparison.} The enabled carrier is
$\{(w,*):P(w)\}\cong\{w:P(w)\}$ by projection. Because both action coordinates are $*$, the product-update relation
reduces to $wR_iv$ on the retained endpoints.
  \item \textbf{Communication and delivery.} Pointed action
quantification along its enabling inclusion is therefore exactly the
comprehension quantification of
\cref{def:egt-public-announcement}; the displayed reduction is the
singleton instance of \cref{agt-prop-action} (equivalently
\cref{thm:egt-public-update-reduction}).
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Institutional and epistemic composition coherence}

For three execution spans, both bracketings have witness carrier
\[
 \{(e,f,g):t_E(e)=s_F(f),\ t_F(f)=s_G(g)\}.
\]
For three composed executions, both bracketings have the same
matched triple of witnesses. Permission is
$P_E(e)\wedge P_F(f)\wedge P_G(g)$, and the concurrent realizer is
$\rho_G(g)\rho_F(f)\rho_E(e)$. Reassociating the witnesses
preserves these fields. The epistemic comparison replaces record
matching by enabled event matching and uses the same dependent-sum and
-product coherence. Thus repeated updates do not require a new
composition law.
Thus the extraction of action events from execution witnesses is
completed only after the finite causal protocol and session adequacy
results of Section~\ref{sec:paper-10}; see
Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data}.


\part{Operational and strategic communication}

\section{True-Concurrent Communication Between Agents}\label{sec:paper-10}

An epistemic update specifies what each recipient can distinguish after an exchange.
A protocol must also explain how the information arrives. We wire finite response
strategies to data ports and use secured interaction to identify the sends and
receives that match. The event structure allows independent decisions to proceed
before the collector has all its inputs. Complete policies retain what each owner
would do on branches that the exchange leaves unvisited. Binary sessions describe
the same obligations at a pair of dual endpoints. The finite causal protocols
also supply an explicit multiplayer arena whose players are these owners.
Both protocol constructions supply the delivery witnesses used in the next section.

\subsection{Agents implemented by causal decision protocols}

\begin{definition}[Decision generators and generated presentations]
\label{def:egt-decision-generators-and-generated-presentations}
Use the locally fully faithful
nonstrategic embedding $\mathbf j_N$ of
Equation~\eqref{eq:egt-nonstrategic-embedding}. For finite $O,A$ and $i\in N$,
define the singly owned decision presentation
\[
 \mathsf{Dec}_i(O,A):D(O)\longrightarrow D(A)
\]
by
\[
 \Sigma_i=A^O,\qquad \Sigma_j=1\ (j\ne i),\qquad
 \pi\longmapsto\widehat\pi.
\]
Let $\mathbf{DecArena}_N(\mathcal C)$ be the smallest locally full symmetric
monoidal sub-bicategory of $\mathbf{Arena}_N(\mathcal C)$ that contains the
image of $\mathbf j_N$ and all finite decision presentations, is closed under
horizontal composition and tensor, is closed under the cartesian parameter
reindexings of Equation~\eqref{eq:egt-owned-reindexing}, and contains every
presentation invertibly $2$-isomorphic to one already generated. Thus a
restriction or duplication of policy descriptions remains in the generated
class only through an exhibited parameter map; it is not silently absorbed
into the word ``decision.'' This gives an explicit meaning to ``generated by
singly owned decisions and nonstrategic wiring.''
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Compact structure of generated decision presentations]
\label{cor:egt-generated-compact}
The bicategory $\mathbf{DecArena}_N(\mathcal C)$ has the coherent
object duals of Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-owned-compact}. Its quotient
by invertible $2$-cells is compact closed. Compact transposition,
the closed hom-category equivalences, and the owner-preserving
trace restrict to this generated bicategory.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Locate the compact generators.} The entire image
of $\mathbf j_N$ belongs to the generated bicategory, so it
contains every original arena and its dual, together with their
coevaluations, evaluations and symmetry maps.
  \item \textbf{Close the bending constructions.} The formulas
for transposition, closed transposition and trace use the given
presentation once, tensor and sequential composition, and these
nonstrategic compact maps. They therefore remain in the generated
class. Local fullness retains the snake and coherence
$2$-isomorphisms. Quotienting gives the compact equations.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Finite causal decision protocol]
\label{def:egt-finite-causal-decision-protocol}
A \textbf{finite causal decision protocol} consists of a finite acyclic
directed graph of decision nodes $V$, an ownership map $i:V\to N$,
finite nonempty action sets $A_v$ for $v\in V$, a finite set $P_0$
of external ports with finite value sets $(X_p)_{p\in P_0}$, and
specified typed input wires. Each incoming wire $e$ of a node $v$
has source either an external port $p$ (carrier $X_e=X_p$) or an
earlier decision node $u$ (carrier $X_e=A_u$); the wires from nodes
respect the directed acyclic graph. If $I_v$ is the finite set of
incoming wires to $v$, its input carrier and raw observation map are
\[
 H_v=\prod_{e\in I_v}X_e,\qquad
 \widetilde o_v:H_v\to Y_v,\qquad
 H_v\xrightarrow{o_v}O_v\hookrightarrow Y_v,
 \quad O_v=\operatorname{im}(\widetilde o_v).
\]
The effective observation quotient $o_v$ determines the node policies
$\pi_v:O_v\to A_v$ and the complete owner policy spaces
\[
 \Sigma_i=\prod_{v:\,i(v)=i}A_v^{O_v}.
\]
The protocol also specifies an outcome function on its full institutional
record (external data together with all node actions),
\[
 z:\left(\prod_{p\in P_0}X_p\right)\times
    \left(\prod_{v\in V}A_v\right)\longrightarrow Z.
\]
The value of $z$ can be corestricted to its finite image for the
concurrent response protocol. An action at $v$ is
$a_v=\pi_v(o_v((x_e)_{e\in I_v}))$. The graph determines which
observations are available at each decision; recording an action for
an institution does not create an additional observation wire.
The generated arena is constructed and its scheduling independence
proved below.
\end{definition}

A finite causal decision protocol makes the origin of each
observation explicit. Nodes respond to the values arriving along their
incoming wires; independent nodes remain concurrent. The owned
realization assigns a complete contingent function to every decision
node, so a policy includes responses at nodes not encountered during a
particular execution. The ensuing construction connects these policies
to secured event-structure strategies.

\begin{lemma}[Decision-event path reflection in a finite protocol]
\label{lem:egt-protocol-event-path}
Fix the external inputs and a complete owner-policy profile of a finite
causal decision protocol. Form its secured interaction with all wired
occurrences still displayed, before hiding the internal channels. In a
completed configuration let $d_v$ be the positive action-output
occurrence at decision node $v$. If $u\ne v$ and $d_u<d_v$ in the
induced causal order, then the protocol DAG contains a nonempty
directed path from $u$ to $v$. Consequently the chosen action outputs
of incomparable nodes are concurrent in this completed interaction.
Hiding preserves this path restriction on any distinct decision-output
occurrences retained as visible events.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Local causal generators.} Expand each response and
collector in the protocol into its source event structure. On a
completed input branch, a response has only its negative-input to
positive-output dependency. A collector has exactly its individual
input-to-tuple-output dependencies, with no dependency between its
distinct inputs. A copying strategy has an input-to-each-output
dependency, with no order between copied outputs. Disposal has no
output. These descriptions are the explicit constructions of
\cref{prop:egt-functions,prop:egt-data-comonoid,prop:egt-finite-collectors}.
  \item \textbf{Paths through secured matching.} In secured
synchronization, each matched internal event is identified with its
input/output occurrence on the adjoining components. The secured
order is the transitive closure of the component orders, and is
acyclic by the secured-matching condition. Hence every strict causal
comparison in the unhidden completed interaction is witnessed by a
finite chain of local generator edges and matched wire occurrences.
The other occurrence of a matched channel cannot insert an edge from
its output backwards to its input.
  \item \textbf{Reflection into the protocol DAG.} Mark each generator
edge that crosses from a decision output towards the next decision
input by its specified protocol wire. Edges inside copying or
collection boxes only progress towards their outputs. Traversing a
chain from $d_u$ to $d_v$, each passage through a decision component
other than the starting one must enter that component through one of
its specified incoming wires and leave through its response output.
Removing the segments within components therefore gives a directed
walk from $u$ to $v$ in the protocol DAG, which is a directed path
because the graph is acyclic. External inputs are sources and the
final institutional collector is a sink, so neither can introduce a
return path between decision nodes.
  \item \textbf{Incomparability and hiding.} If $u$ and $v$ are
incomparable, neither $d_u<d_v$ nor $d_v<d_u$ can hold. Both
occurrences belong to the completed configuration and are therefore
consistent, so they are concurrent. Hiding restricts the transitive
secured order to visible occurrences; a newly visible comparison
between retained decision outputs would already be a comparison in
the expanded interaction, which has just been excluded.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Coherence and scheduling independence of finite causal decision protocols]
\label{thm:egt-causal-protocol}
Every finite causal decision protocol determines an open arena in
$\mathbf{DecArena}_N(\mathcal C)$. For each external input and policy profile it
has a unique completed action assignment satisfying
\[
 a_v=\pi_v\bigl(o_v((a_u)_{u\to v},\text{incoming external data})\bigr).
\]
Every evaluation along a linear extension of the causal order yields that
assignment. In the concurrent realization, incomparable decision components
remain unordered; a linear extension is only a reading of the same
symmetric-monoidal diagram.
\end{theorem}

\noindent Independent nodes can each produce an output. The collector can emit the
pair only after both outputs have arrived.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
D(M_v)\otimes D(M_w)\arrow[r,"c_{M_v,M_w}"]\arrow[d,"\widehat f\otimes\widehat g"']
 &D(M_v\times M_w)\arrow[d,"\widehat{f\times g}"]\\
 D(N_v)\otimes D(N_w)\arrow[r,"c_{N_v,N_w}"']&D(N_v\times N_w)
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}


\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Build the owned wiring.} Route each value to its specified
recipients with the data comonoid of
Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-data-comonoid}, using disposal for zero
recipients. At decision node $v$ insert
\[
 \bigotimes_{e\in I_v}D(X_e)
 \xrightarrow{c_v}D(H_v)
 \xrightarrow{\widehat{o_v}}D(O_v)
 \xrightarrow{\widehat{\pi_v}}D(A_v),
\]
with the nullary collector $c_0:I\to D(1)$ when $I_v$ is empty.
Copy the action to its successor and institutional-record wires; collect
the full record and apply the response for the finite image of $z$.
Every box is nonstrategic wiring or a singly owned decision generator.
Grouping the latter's parameters by owner gives exactly $\Sigma_i$,
so the diagram belongs to $\mathbf{DecArena}_N(\mathcal C)$.
  \item \textbf{Solve the policy equations.} Induct on causal height.
At a minimal node the incoming values are external; at any later node
they have already been determined. Applying $o_v$ and then $\pi_v$
therefore determines a unique $a_v$. The same induction proves that
every solution, and every evaluation along a linear extension, has
these values.
  \item \textbf{Compare readings of the diagram.} Causal height gives
a layered expression using tensor within layers and composition between
layers. Any two linear extensions differ by adjacent swaps of
incomparable nodes: move the first node of one extension past its
incomparable predecessors in the other, and iterate. Each swap is
monoidal interchange. Symmetry and associativity compare the remaining
enumerations and bracketings, and coassociativity and cocommutativity
compare copying trees. Thus all readings denote the same concurrent
arrow.
  \item \textbf{Retain independence of events.} Equality of completed
values alone would not establish the causal claim.
Lemma~\ref{lem:egt-protocol-event-path} proves that a causal comparison
between distinct decision outputs in the expanded secured interaction
requires a directed path in the protocol DAG. Incomparable decisions
therefore remain concurrent, including when their outputs are retained
through hiding. The linear extension is an external reading of this
diagram and inserts no scheduling event or causal edge.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
\text{incoming data at }v \arrow[r,"o_v"] & O_v
 \arrow[r,"\pi_v"] & A_v \arrow[d,"\text{specified wires}"] \\
&& \text{later observations and outcome records}
\end{tikzcd}
\caption{A policy receives its constructed observation quotient. Wiring can
retain additional records without making them available to that policy.}
\end{figure}

The protocol construction now identifies complete economic policies
with families of operational response functions. Each function uses the
effective observation at its own node, and its realization is receptive
and courteous. When several nodes belong to one owner, the resulting
policy is their product; ownership neither duplicates the process nor
orders otherwise independent events. This provides a concrete
implementation of the agent representation.

\begin{remark}[Protocol coherence and incentives]
The linear-logical account of multiparty protocol compatibility in
\citet{CarboneEtAl2015,CarboneEtAl2016} concerns the operational layer.
In the present construction, the causal protocol specifies the agents' implemented interactions,
while preference comparisons and profitable deviations determine incentive
properties. Section~\ref{agt-sec-equilibrium} constructs the latter;
the multiplayer comparison below identifies them on the implemented
player strategies.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Multiplayer game semantics of the agents}
\label{sec:egt-multiplayer-semantics}

The finite protocol now determines a game whose players are the owners
and whose complete strategies are their policies. Partial plays record
causal assignments, local response interfaces enforce the observation
quotients, and secured interaction computes the implemented outcome.
The comparison with \cref{thm:egt-causal-protocol} will also identify
legal deviations and the resulting equilibrium predicates.

The compositional category is already supplied by
\cref{thm:egt-owned-compact,cor:egt-generated-compact}: operational
arenas are its objects and owned multiplayer systems are its morphisms.
The owner-labelled event structures constructed here present their
finite partial plays. The retained-event isomorphism of
Lemma~\ref{lem:egt-multiplayer-retained-comparison} connects those
plays to the expanded concurrent implementation, while compact
transposition and feedback retain every owner's complete policy set.

There are direct precedents for these structures. The multi-agent
semantics of \citet{Abramsky2007MultiAgent} uses agent-labelled concrete
domains, closure-operator strategies, and least common fixed points for
interaction. Partial-order Boolean games and their finite-action
extension assign collections of decision nodes to players and retain
their contingent responses
\citep{BradfieldEtAl2016PartialOrder,ZahoranskyEtAl2022PartialOrder}.
We construct the comparison using the effective observation quotients,
complete owner policies, and concurrent implementation already specified
here. Information restrictions must be retained at the strategy
interface: access levels in \citet{ClairambaultEtAl2013Imperfect} give a
related way of excluding responses that wait for unavailable information.

\subsubsection{Ownership and operational polarity}

An owner label specifies who may replace a complete strategy. Polarity
specifies input and output responsibility at an operational boundary.
They enter different parts of the construction. In particular, grouping
owners does not repolarize their implemented components.

\begin{example}[Repolarizing a coalition can destroy courtesy]
\label{ex:egt-coalition-repolarization}
Let $E$ have two independent events $a,b$, owned by $1,2$ respectively.
In player $1$'s view, make $a$ positive and $b$ negative, and take the
strategy with both events independent. In player $2$'s view, make $a$
negative and $b$ positive, and take the strategy with $a<b$.
Both strategies are receptive and courteous: the second introduces
only a negative-to-positive dependency.

Their unpolarized secured pullback has $a<b$. Declaring both events
positive for the coalition $\{1,2\}$ makes its inclusion into the
original independent arena noncourteous, since it introduces a
positive-to-positive immediate dependency. Thus interaction followed by
coalition recolouring does not define the required operation in $\cC$.
The construction below retains explicit local interfaces; regrouping
changes their policy control, while their polarities and wiring remain
the operational ones of \cref{thm:egt-causal-protocol}.
\end{example}

\subsubsection{The arena of causal assignments}

Fix a finite causal decision protocol $\mathcal P$ as in
\cref{def:egt-finite-causal-decision-protocol}. Put $T=P_0\sqcup V$
and $A_p=X_p$ for $p\in P_0$. Let $\preceq$ be the partial order
generated by its specified typed input wires. Repeated wires from one
source remain repeated coordinates in $H_v$; they do not create new
source decisions. The effective observation $o_v:H_v\twoheadrightarrow
O_v$ may forget a value even when its arrival is a prerequisite of
the decision.

\begin{construction}[Value-labelled causal occurrences]
\label{con:egt-multiplayer-arena}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{Form the events.}
An event is a pair
\[
 (t,\alpha),\qquad t\in T,\qquad
 \alpha\in\prod_{s\preceq t}A_s.
\]
It records the value at $t$ together with its causal history.
\item \textbf{Order and compare histories.}
Set
\[
 (s,\beta)\leq(t,\alpha)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 s\preceq t\ \text{ and }\ \beta=\alpha|_{\downarrow s}.
\]
Two events conflict when their assignments disagree on the intersection
of their domains. A finite set is consistent when all its assignments
agree on overlaps.
\item \textbf{Display control.}
Give $(v,\alpha)$ its owner label and external-input events a separate
environment label in $N\sqcup\{\mathsf{env}\}$. Denote the resulting
owner-labelled event structure by $E_{\mathcal P}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{lemma}[Configurations and independent extensions]
\label{lem:egt-multiplayer-configurations}
The arena $E_{\mathcal P}$ is a finite prime event structure, with an
order isomorphism
\[
 \operatorname{Conf}(E_{\mathcal P})
 \cong
 \left\{(D,a):D\subseteq T\text{ downclosed},\quad
                       a\in\prod_{t\in D}A_t\right\},
\]
where the right side is ordered by extension of partial assignments.
If two distinct decision nodes are enabled at one partial assignment,
assigning either does not change the other's input. Any prescribed
choices at these nodes have a common extension in either execution order.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{Verify the event structure.}
Restriction makes the event order reflexive, transitive, and
antisymmetric. The predecessors of $(t,\alpha)$ are exactly
$(s,\alpha|_{\downarrow s})$ for $s\preceq t$, hence are finite
and mutually consistent. Disagreement persists under extension of either
history, so conflict is hereditary. Consistency is closed under subsets
and adjoining causal predecessors.
\item \textbf{Recover the partial assignment.}
For a configuration, agreement on overlaps makes the union of its
histories a function $a$. Its domain $D$ is downclosed. Conversely,
\[
 (D,a)\longmapsto
 \{(t,a|_{\downarrow t}):t\in D\}
\]
is a configuration. The two constructions are inverse and preserve order.
\item \textbf{Commute independent decisions.}
If one enabled but unassigned node preceded the other, the latter would
not be enabled. They are therefore incomparable, with all predecessors
already assigned. Their extensions agree on the common history and
assign different new nodes, so their union is a configuration.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

The absence of a race between distinct enabled decision nodes follows
from the protocol construction. It requires no extra restriction on the
finite protocols of \cref{def:egt-finite-causal-decision-protocol}.

\subsubsection{Complete strategies and local response interfaces}

\begin{definition}[Complete multiplayer strategy]
\label{def:egt-multiplayer-strategy}
A complete strategy for player $i$ is a family of total responses
$r_v:H_v\to A_v$, one for each $v$ owned by $i$, constant on the
fibres of $o_v$. Thus its strategy space is
\[
 \mathsf{Str}_i(\mathcal P)=
 \prod_{v:\,i(v)=i}
 \{r_v:H_v\to A_v:\ker(o_v)\subseteq\ker(r_v)\}.
\]
The same player controls the entire family. The observation quotient
specifies which distinctions each response may use.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Complete strategies are exactly the agent policies]
\label{prop:egt-multiplayer-strategies}
There are canonical bijections
\[
 \mathcal R_i:\Sigma_i=
 \prod_{v:\,i(v)=i}A_v^{O_v}
 \xrightarrow{\cong}\mathsf{Str}_i(\mathcal P),
 \qquad (\pi_v)_v\longmapsto(\pi_vo_v)_v.
\]
These complete strategies are faithfully implemented by the families
$(\widehat{\pi_v}:D(O_v)\to D(A_v))_{i(v)=i}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{Factor the response through observation.}
For an invariant response $r_v$, the relation
\[
 \{(o,a):\exists h\in H_v\,
            (o_v(h)=o\ \wedge\ r_v(h)=a)\}
\]
is total by surjectivity of $o_v$ and single-valued by invariance.
It defines the unique $\pi_v:O_v\to A_v$ with $r_v=\pi_vo_v$.
No choice of representatives of observation classes is required.
Taking the product over the owner's nodes proves the bijection.
\item \textbf{Recover every local response.}
By \cref{prop:egt-functions}, the response strategy
$\widehat{\pi_v}$ contains the prescribed output $\pi_v(o)$ at
each input $o$. An isomorphism over the labelled arena preserves these
responses. The whole family therefore recovers every component of the
complete policy, including responses not used in a selected execution.
\qedhere
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

The owner process can be displayed as
\[
 R_i(\pi_i)=\bigotimes_{v:\,i(v)=i}\widehat{\pi_v}:
 \bigotimes_{v:\,i(v)=i}D(O_v)
 \longrightarrow\bigotimes_{v:\,i(v)=i}D(A_v),
\]
with the node interfaces retained. The protocol supplies the prescribed
observed input at each interface. An arbitrary arrow between the two
tensor boundaries could introduce additional information dependencies;
the complete strategies here are the displayed families of finite
response strategies. This functional fragment uses the existing
concurrent category, consistently with the comparisons of functional
models and concurrent strategies in \citet{Winskel2023}.

\begin{proposition}[Operational projection of a player's strategy]
\label{prop:egt-multiplayer-pruning}
Polarize $E_{\mathcal P}$ positively on owner $i$ and negatively on
the other labels, obtaining $E_{\mathcal P}^{(i)}$. Let $S_i(\pi_i)$
be the induced substructure of events whose histories satisfy every
$i$-owned policy equation occurring in them. Its inclusion into
$E_{\mathcal P}^{(i)}$ is receptive and courteous. Every conflict
between its histories has a disagreement at a negative event in its
causal past; there is no independent positive choice left by the policy.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{Restrict histories.}
The selected event set is downclosed: every equation in a predecessor
history occurs in the larger history. It inherits the event structure
and introduces no new immediate causal edge, proving courtesy.
\item \textbf{Accept the environment's enabled moves.}
If a negative event is enabled above a selected configuration, its
predecessors already satisfy the owner's equations. Its own node is
not controlled by $i$, so its history is selected as well. The inclusion
gives a unique lift, proving receptivity.
\item \textbf{Locate the origin of a conflict.}
For two conflicting histories, choose a $\preceq$-minimal node at
which their values differ. All predecessor values agree. The node
cannot belong to $i$, since the fixed policy applied to the same
observation gives the same value. It is therefore negative.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[Off-path policies survive their operational projection]
\label{ex:egt-multiplayer-offpath}
Let one owner control $u\prec v$, choose $u=0$, and let $v$ observe
$u$. Two policies agreeing at $v(0)$ but differing at $v(1)$ give
the same $S_i(\pi_i)$: the earlier choice has already removed the
branch $u=1$. The complete local response family still distinguishes
them, since its component at $v$ accepts input $1$ and records the
prescribed response. Thus the global pruning describes execution, while
the family of \cref{prop:egt-multiplayer-strategies} retains the
complete strategy.

Repeated wires can also make some tuples in $H_v$ structurally
unreachable. The declared response still has its entire domain $O_v$.
Institutional tests on those entries remain well defined; neither
pruning nor an extensive-form unfolding may silently discard them.
\end{example}

\subsubsection{Secured interaction and compilation}

Fix external data $u\in U_{\mathrm{ext}}=\prod_{p\in P_0}X_p$
and a complete profile $\pi$. Let $S_{\mathsf{env}}(u)$ select the histories
agreeing with $u$ at every external port in their domain. Forget
polarity on the strategy views, so all inclusions have codomain
$E_{\mathcal P}$.

\begin{theorem}[Multiplayer interaction and its concurrent implementation]
\label{thm:egt-multiplayer-interaction}
The multiway secured interaction is canonically
\[
 E_{u,\pi}=S_{\mathsf{env}}(u)\cap\bigcap_{i\in N}S_i(\pi_i)
 \hookrightarrow E_{\mathcal P}.
\]
It has a unique maximal configuration, whose assignment is the
completed solution of \cref{thm:egt-causal-protocol}. Every maximal
sequence of enabled extensions reaches it, and independent decision
occurrences remain concurrent. Connecting the complete local response
families through that theorem's wiring realizes exactly its concurrent
arrow $g_\pi$. In the fully supplied unhidden implementation, the
order between decision outputs is the restriction of $\preceq$ to
the decision nodes.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{Identify the secured pullback.}
All maps are inclusions of downclosed substructures with the inherited
order. Matching requires identical labelled events; the combined
order is already the acyclic order of $E_{\mathcal P}$. All such
diagonal matchings are secured. Their pullback is the intersection:
every compatible family of maps has image there and factors uniquely
through it. This also proves associativity under regrouping.
\item \textbf{Construct the completed play.}
At external nodes the values are $u$. By induction on causal height,
the predecessor values determine the raw input, its observation, and
\[
 a_v=\pi_v\bigl(o_v((a_{\operatorname{src}(e)})_{e\in I_v})\bigr).
\]
This constructs a full compatible assignment. Every partial assignment
in the interaction is its restriction, by the same induction. A proper
partial assignment has a minimal missing node and extends at that node,
so it is not maximal. Finiteness implies that every maximal sequence
of genuine extensions reaches the full assignment. The independent
extensions commute by \cref{lem:egt-multiplayer-configurations}.
\item \textbf{Compare the implemented components.}
At each node use exactly
\[
 \bigotimes_{e\in I_v}D(X_e)
 \xrightarrow{c_v}D(H_v)
 \xrightarrow{\widehat{o_v}}D(O_v)
 \xrightarrow{\widehat{\pi_v}}D(A_v).
\]
The nullary case uses $c_0$. Copying routes the chosen value to the
specified successors and record wires, and the final collector and
response compute $z$. Thus the local equations and completed outcome
are those of the preceding step. If $K$ denotes this fixed wiring,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:egt-multiplayer-compilation}
 K[(\widehat{\pi_v})_{v\in V}]=g_\pi.
\end{equation}
Both sides are the same symmetric-monoidal composite, so this is equality
of concurrent arrows, not only agreement of output values.
\item \textbf{Compare causal orders.}
Every specified wire from $u$ to $v$ supplies a causal path from
$d_u$ through copying, reception, and collection to $d_v$.
Conversely, the local-generator analysis in
\cref{lem:egt-protocol-event-path} projects every path between
decision outputs to specified dependency wires. The induced order is
therefore exactly the wire-generated order $\preceq$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

The owner-labelled interaction is an unpolarized secured pullback; its
player views are not asserted to be pairwise dual arenas. Its
implementation uses the original polarized response interfaces and
composition in $\cC$. The expanded implementation retains receipt,
copying, collection, and any further institutional occurrences. The
smaller arena $E_{\mathcal P}$ records the input and decision
occurrences. These are distinct presentations: the expanded witnesses
remain available for the information and measured-execution tests.

\begin{lemma}[Retained-event comparison with multiplayer partial plays]
\label{lem:egt-multiplayer-retained-comparison}
For a finite causal decision protocol and $x=(u,\pi)$, let $a^x$
be its completed assignment. In the fully supplied unhidden
implementation $Q_x$, let $J_x$ consist of the external-source
occurrence $e_p$ for each external port and the action-output
occurrence $e_v$ for each decision node. There is a canonical
event-structure isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:egt-multiplayer-retained-comparison}
 \theta_x:E_{u,\pi}\xrightarrow{\cong}Q_x|J_x,
 \qquad(t,a^x|_{\downarrow t})\longmapsto e_t.
\end{equation}
The induced configuration comparison
\[
 p_x:\operatorname{Conf}(Q_x)\longrightarrow
      \operatorname{Conf}(E_{u,\pi}),\qquad
 p_x(k)=\theta_x^{-1}[k\cap J_x]
\]
is surjective and bounded for retained one-event extensions and
their weak implementations through hidden occurrences.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
