The old and new joint action-event images and enabling carriers are
canonically isomorphic.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Read the appended receipt.} In the canonical
compiler every old designated recipient occurrence precedes the
terminal full-record report: its outgoing path reaches a decision
or record component feeding the final collector. The new recipient
receipt follows that report. Its fixed label and value $r$ append
one observed occurrence after the old local record. The resulting
labelled-poset class is determined by, and recovers,
$(d_i^{\mathrm{old}},r)$.
  \item \textbf{Identify the joint images.} The map
\[
 (r,(v_i)_i)\longmapsto(r,((v_i,r))_i)
\]
is bijective onto the new joint image, with inverse given by
projection. It preserves the source world under the completed-run
bijection. Taking the world-and-event images therefore identifies
the enabled carriers as well.
  \item \textbf{Calculate the updated knowledge relation.}
Equality of the new observation tuple is exactly equality of its
three coordinates, proving \eqref{eq:egt-public-delivered-kernel}.
The completion boundary follows all acknowledgements, so the record
asserts actual receipt at every owner. This realizes the public
observation used in epistemic product update
\citep{BaltagMossSolecki1998PublicAnnouncements}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent Public delivery enlarges each recipient record while
preserving the joint action image up to its canonical identification.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \Xi^{\mathrm{pub}}\arrow[r,"\cong"]\arrow[d,"q^{\mathrm{pub}}"',two heads]
 &\Xi^{\mathrm{old}}\arrow[d,"q^{\mathrm{old}}",two heads]\\
 E^{\mathrm{pub}}\arrow[r,"\cong"']&E^{\mathrm{old}}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

For an implementation with additional activity concurrent with the
old report, use the actual full induced recipient poset. It retains
the relative order of old and new receipts, which the pair formula
alone need not encode. The broadcast circuit still witnesses public
delivery, and the observation is formed from this complete delivered
record. In the following sheaf comparisons, $V_i,d_i,b_i$ always
denote the effective actual records, including the public receipt
when public delivery is specified. An output exported only to an
external evaluator does not add a recipient observation.


\subsection{Sheaf-local presentations of completed communication}
\label{sec:sheaf-implemented-witnesses}

The completed witness carrier $\Xi$ constructed above can now be
compared with the policy-indexed sheaf of
Section~\ref{sec:sheaf-owned-witnesses}.  The comparison uses the
already exhibited fully expanded secured histories, before hiding.
It does not infer a received message from the mere existence of an
outgoing signal.  The connection between global task solutions and
compatible local information in \citet{FelberEtAl2025} is a related
perspective; here the task and its witnesses are those of the existing
finite true-concurrent protocol.

\begin{construction}[Finite protocol witness site and completion subobject]
\label{con:sheaf-finite-protocol}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Retain the expanded concurrent histories.} Let
$X=U_{\mathrm{ext}}\times\Sigma$ be the finite external-input
and complete-policy carrier of a fixed finite causal protocol of
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-causal-protocol}. For public delivery, include
the circuit of Construction~\ref{con:egt-witnessed-public-broadcast}
in the expansion and use its final output as completion boundary.
It adds no policy coordinates and preserves the terminal report.
For each $x\in X$ retain the resulting finite expanded
secured-interaction event structure $Q_x$ before hiding.
Write $\Xi_{\mathrm{in},x}$ for the configurations with
the protocol's designated completed terminal record.  These retain
the actual event witnesses.  Any further independent institutional
certificate family of Section~\ref{sec:egt-witnesses} remains
separately indexed; it is not inferred from a matching graph.
  \item \textbf{Give the family a common interface.} Form the
finite disjoint-union event structure $E=\bigsqcup_{x\in X}Q_x$,
forgetting polarities for the matching comparison.  Take
$f_x=g_x=\iota_x:Q_x\hookrightarrow E$, the tagged inclusions.
A secured matching of the two copies of $Q_x$ over $E$ is exactly the
diagonal of a configuration $z$ of $Q_x$:
\[
 \mathcal M(\iota_x,\iota_x)
 \cong\operatorname{Conf}(Q_x),\qquad
 z\longmapsto\{(e,e):e\in z\}.
\]
Thus the common-family site of
Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-owned-site} gives a sheaf of precisely
the exhibited concurrent histories, with no new process constructor.
  \item \textbf{Choose the completion boundary.} Denote by
$F_x\subseteq|Q_x|$ the labelled final-report occurrences of the
protocol.  Form the saturated anchor $A$ containing their images in
$E$, the designated recipient receipt occurrences, and institutional
certificate occurrences.  Define the predicate on matching sections
\[
 \mathsf{Finished}(x,\varphi)
 \iff\text{a designated final-report event in $F_x$ occurs in $\varphi$.}
\]
On the anchored site put
$\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}(V)
 =\{k\in\mathscr K_A(V):\mathsf{Finished}(k)\}$.
The uniqueness of the completed action assignment in
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-causal-protocol} constructs its terminal outcome
map $z_X:X\to Z$.  For the already specified institutional
acceptance predicate $Q\hookrightarrow Z$, put
\[
 X_Q=z_X^{-1}(Q),\qquad
 \mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{acc}}
 =\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}
  \times_{\underline X}\underline{X_Q}.
\]
The complete input and policy parameter stays fixed on causal
restriction, so this is the accepted-history subobject.  To derive
actual authorization from the exhibited protocol, define $R_x$ as the finite set of issuer-output/recipient-input
wire incidences at the authorization ports already exhibited in
the finite protocol (so no independent role list is postulated), and let
$\mathsf{Tok}_r(k)$ be the set of events of the anchored matching
$k=(x,\varphi)$ which are the secured synchronizations of the
specified issuer output and corresponding recipient input in role
$r\in R_x$.  Such an event retains its prime secured causal history;
a token-shaped but unmatched label does not belong to this set.
Construct the dependent token-proof carrier and its image
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-token-incidence}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf{TokProof}(k)&=\prod_{r\in R_x}\mathsf{Tok}_r(k),\\
 J_A&=\coprod_{k\in\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}(A)}\mathsf{TokProof}(k),\\
 C_A&=\im(J_A\xrightarrow{j_A}\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}(A)).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The factors are subobjects of the exhibited secured-event incidence
sets, so $J_A$ and $C_A$ are constructed from the actual wiring.
The finite product enforces all designated token roles, while
$J_A$ retains distinct issuer/recipient witnesses.  Define
\[
 \mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{auth}}
 =\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{acc}}
 \times_{\underline{\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}(A)}}
 \underline{C_A}.
\]
Because $A$ contains the token occurrences and their causal past,
restriction to $A$ preserves and reflects these synchronizations.
The pullback therefore tests actual authorization and institutional
acceptance together.  Independent certificate objects remain
proof-relevant, as in
Construction~\ref{con:egt-general-witness-family}, rather than being
identified with issuer events.
  \item \textbf{Read actual received subhistories.} For a
configuration in $Q_x$, the recipient record is the isomorphism
class of the induced receiver poset, labelled by fixed protocol
port occurrences and delivered values as in
Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data}. The tag $x$ in
$E=\bigsqcup_xQ_x$ remains part of the execution witness and
retained parameter, but is not an additional recipient label.
Public reports use the designated actual broadcast receptions.  The institutional
record retains the issuer-produced token occurrence and the matched
recipient occurrence, with the causal data in their saturated past.
These are functions of $k|_A$.  On completed configurations they agree
with the previously constructed delivery maps $d_i:\Xi_W\to V_i$
after the ordinary world-index pullback
and with the institutional certificate record.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{proposition}[Explicit finite anchor, port readouts, and token witnesses]
\label{prop:sheaf-finite-port-readout}
In Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-finite-protocol}, let $H\subseteq E$
be the union of the final-report, designated recipient and token
occurrences, and let $A$ be its least simultaneously saturated patch.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-finite-anchor-explicit}
 A=\downarrow_EH.
\end{equation}
In particular, $A=E$ exactly when every occurrence of $E$ is
causally below a designated member of $H$; in that case the anchored
site has the single object $E$.

Let $\kappa:\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}\xrightarrow{\cong}\mathscr F(E)$
be the map sending a completed configuration $z$ in $Q_x$ to
$(x,\{(e,e):e\in z\})$, and write
$\rho_A:\mathscr F(E)\to\mathscr F(A)$ for restriction.
For each designated recipient and for the public output, the actual
completed port-readout functions of
Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data} factor as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-finite-readout-comparison}
 d_i=\operatorname{rec}_{i,A}\,\rho_A\,\kappa,
 \qquad
 d_0=\operatorname{rec}_{0,A}\,\rho_A\,\kappa.
\end{equation}
The issuer/recipient proof carrier $J_A\to\mathscr F(A)$ of
\eqref{eq:sheaf-token-incidence} constructs a proof-relevant sheaf
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-token-witness-sheaf}
 \mathscr W_{\mathrm{tok}}
 =\mathscr F\times_{\underline{\mathscr F(A)}}\underline{J_A}
 \longrightarrow\mathscr F.
\end{equation}
Its image is precisely the anchored token-certificate subobject,
\[
 \operatorname{im}(\mathscr W_{\mathrm{tok}}\to\mathscr F)
 =\mathscr F\times_{\underline{\mathscr F(A)}}\underline{C_A},
 \qquad
 \Gamma(\mathscr W_{\mathrm{tok}})
 \cong\mathscr F(E)\times_{\mathscr F(A)}J_A.
\]
Pulling the same construction back to
$\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{acc}}$ gives the actually authorized sheaf
$\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{auth}}$ as its image, without identifying
distinct token witnesses.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Since $E=\bigsqcup_xQ_x$ and $f_x=g_x=\iota_x$, the source-
and target-predecessor images in the anchor operator are contained
in $\downarrow_EU$ for every $U\subseteq E$; conversely
$\downarrow_EU$ is a summand of that operator.  Hence
$\Phi_H(U)=H\cup\downarrow_EU$.  Starting at $\varnothing$
gives $U_1=H$, $U_2=\downarrow_EH$, and
$U_3=U_2$.  This proves \eqref{eq:sheaf-finite-anchor-explicit}
and its characterization of the anchored site.

For each $x$, both projections of the diagonal matching have
configuration $z$, and their combined secured order is exactly
the order of $Q_x$ restricted to $z$.  The inverse of $\kappa$
therefore forgets the redundant second coordinate and is canonical.
By construction every designated recipient and public occurrence
lies in $A$.  Since $A$ is downward closed, its restriction retains
every causal predecessor of those occurrences.  Taking their
induced port-and-value-labelled order before or after restriction
gives the same record class by
Lemma~\ref{lem:egt-delivered-record-invariance}.  The displayed local policy register,
when present, is a projection from the persistent parameter $x$.
This proves both equations in
\eqref{eq:sheaf-finite-readout-comparison}, without choosing a
linear schedule or a representative of an image quotient.

The two factors in \eqref{eq:sheaf-token-witness-sheaf} are
sheaves; their pullback is a sheaf because limits are computed
objectwise.  Factor the displayed incidence map as the ordinary
regular image $J_A\twoheadrightarrow C_A\hookrightarrow\mathscr F(A)$.
Both constant presheaves are sheaves in the nonempty-cover topology,
and the first map is sectionwise surjective.  Its pullback along
$\mathscr F\to\underline{\mathscr F(A)}$ is therefore a regular
epimorphism, followed by the pullback of the mono.  This is the
claimed image factorization.  Applying global sections, which
preserve pullbacks and satisfy $\Gamma\underline Y=Y$ here,
gives the displayed formula for $\Gamma\mathscr W_{\mathrm{tok}}$.
Finally, intersection with acceptance is a further pullback,
and regular images in the sheaf topos are pullback-stable.
Thus the resulting image is exactly
$\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{acc}}
 \times_{\underline{\mathscr F(A)}}\underline{C_A}$,
which is the already defined authorized sheaf.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Terminal-anchor specialization for the canonical compiler]
\label{prop:sheaf-canonical-terminal-anchor}
For the canonical full-record compiler of
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-causal-protocol}, let $f_x$ be the final-report
occurrence in the fully supplied expansion $Q_x$. Then
\[
 \downarrow_{Q_x}f_x=Q_x,\qquad
 A=E=\bigsqcup_{x\in X}Q_x.
\]
The completed anchored site has one object, and its completed
configuration and retained-record carriers satisfy
\[
 \Xi_{\mathrm{in}}\cong X,\qquad T_{\mathrm{fin}}\cong X,
 \qquad
 q^{\mathrm{fin}}:\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}
                   \xrightarrow{\cong}\underline X.
\]
The same conclusions hold after the witnessed public broadcast of
Construction~\ref{con:egt-witnessed-public-broadcast}, using its
final output as completion boundary.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Follow every occurrence to the final collector.}
Every external value and every decision action has an
institutional-record wire. Each occurrence in a canonical copying
tree feeds either that record or a later decision whose action feeds
the record. Finiteness and acyclicity therefore give a path from
every routed occurrence to the final collector. The observation,
response and collection occurrences lie on these paths; a nullary
collector precedes its decision output. The final response follows
the collected full record. Thus every occurrence lies below $f_x$.
  \item \textbf{Identify the completed configuration and anchor.}
The supplied branches form the finite conflict-free $Q_x$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-multiplayer-weak-lifting}. Its full carrier
is a configuration, and a configuration containing $f_x$ must
contain all of it. There is exactly one completed configuration
$c_x$ over each $x$. The anchor contains every $f_x$ and is
downward closed, so $A=E$. Its only containing patch is $E$.
  \item \textbf{Compute the retained image.} The retained readout
includes $x$. Its completed image therefore has exactly one element
over each $x$, and its quotient is bijective. On the one-object site
this is the stated isomorphism of sheaves. Empty parameter carriers
give the same statements with empty completed carriers. In the
broadcast extension, all acknowledgements and the old final report
precede the new final report, so the argument applies to that boundary.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

This specialization concerns the exhibited canonical compiler.
Independent certificate objects remain in their separate witness
families, and the general construction also permits implementations
with further independent occurrences. The later map
$v_W:T_W\twoheadrightarrow U_W$ can still forget complete policy
data and remains a substantive epistemic quotient even when
$q^{\mathrm{fin}}$ is an isomorphism.

\begin{construction}[Local restrictions of completed canonical runs]
\label{con:sheaf-complete-run-restrictions}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Retain the completed configurations.} Let $c_x$
be the unique completed configuration just constructed. On the
original unanchored common site set
\[
 \mathscr C(U)=\{(x,c_x|_U):x\in X\}
      \hookrightarrow\mathscr K_X(U),
\]
using the diagonal-matching identification of
Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-finite-protocol}.
  \item \textbf{Restrict the completed views.} For $V\subseteq U$,
send $(x,c_x|_U)$ to $(x,c_x|_V)$. The parameter remains fixed;
the displayed event history is its restriction to the smaller patch.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{proposition}[Full-site sheaf of completed-run restrictions]
\label{prop:sheaf-complete-run-restrictions}
The displayed $\mathscr C$ is a sheaf, naturally isomorphic to
$\underline X$, and its inclusion in $\mathscr K_X$ is a natural
monomorphism. Moreover
\[
 \Gamma\mathscr C\cong\Xi_{\mathrm{in}},\qquad
 \mathscr C|_{\mathcal O_A}\cong\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}.
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Identify the sheaf and its inclusion.} The map
$x\mapsto(x,c_x|_U)$ is bijective onto $\mathscr C(U)$ and
natural in $U$. Constant presheaves are sheaves in the nonempty-cover
topology by Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-owned-witness-descent}.
The inclusion into $\mathscr K_X(U)$ is injective because the
parameter is retained, and restriction commutes with that inclusion.
  \item \textbf{Recover completed runs at the terminal patch.}
At $E$, the sections are exactly $(x,c_x)$, identifying global
sections with $\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}$. At the completed anchor $A=E$
these are exactly the finished matching sections. This proves both
displayed identifications.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent The completed-run views retain their parameter while their
exhibited histories restrict along the causal site.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathscr C(U)\arrow[r,hook]\arrow[d,"(-)|_V"']
 &\mathscr K_X(U)\arrow[d,"(-)|_V"]\\
 \mathscr C(V)\arrow[r,hook]&\mathscr K_X(V)
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

A section of $\mathscr C$ is a local view of an already completed
run; it need not contain a final-report occurrence. This differs from
the predicate $\mathsf{Finished}$ on a partial execution. Knowledge
computed from only the receptions on a smaller unanchored patch can
change, as in Example~\ref{ex:sheaf-unanchored-knowledge}. The
completed anchored comparison and the full-site restriction sheaf
therefore retain their respective observation interfaces explicitly.


\begin{proposition}[Exact anchored descent of certificate predicates]
\label{prop:sheaf-certificate-descent}
Write $\mathscr F=\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}$, let $E$ be the full
interface, and let
$\rho_A:\mathscr F(E)\to\mathscr F(A)$ be restriction.
For every global certificate predicate $P\hookrightarrow\mathscr F(E)$,
put $P_A=\operatorname{im}(\rho_A|_P)$ and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-certificate-closure}
 \operatorname{Cl}_A(P)=\rho_A^{-1}(P_A).
\end{equation}
This is the least anchor-determined predicate containing $P$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-certificate-criterion}
\begin{aligned}
 P&=\operatorname{Cl}_A(P),\\
 \operatorname{pr}_1^*P&=\operatorname{pr}_2^*P
 &&\text{on }\mathscr F(E)\times_{\mathscr F(A)}\mathscr F(E),\\
 P&=\rho_A^{-1}(C_A)
 &&\text{for a unique }C_A\subseteq\mathscr F(A).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For any $C_A\subseteq\mathscr F(A)$ the pullback
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-certificate-sheaf}
 \mathscr F^{C_A}
 =\mathscr F\times_{\underline{\mathscr F(A)}}\underline{C_A}
\end{equation}
is a sheaf with
$\Gamma(\mathscr F^{C_A})\cong\rho_A^{-1}(C_A)$.
For $T_{C_A}=\operatorname{im}(d_A|_{C_A})$, its retained-record map
$\mathscr F^{C_A}\twoheadrightarrow\underline{T_{C_A}}$
is a regular epimorphism.  Thus its designated relations have the
source-fixed lifting and modal equations of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-modal-descent}.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Compute the effective-descent criterion.} The map
$\rho_A$ is split surjective: extend an anchored completed matching
to the full interface by the same graph, using
Lemma~\ref{lem:sheaf-retained-surjection}; the final-report event
is retained.  The kernel-pair criterion of
Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-kernel-descent} therefore identifies the
$\rho_A$-invariant predicates exactly with the inverse images of
unique predicates on $\mathscr F(A)$.  Its image $P_A$ gives the least
such predicate containing $P$.  This proves
\eqref{eq:sheaf-certificate-criterion} and makes
$\operatorname{Cl}_A$ extensive, monotone and idempotent.
  \item \textbf{Construct the certificate sheaf.} Restriction to $A$
defines a natural map
$\mathscr F\to\underline{\mathscr F(A)}$.  Both constant
presheaves in \eqref{eq:sheaf-certificate-sheaf} are sheaves by
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-owned-witness-descent}.  Their pullback is
therefore a sheaf.  At the terminal patch $E$, its elements are
exactly the completed histories whose anchor lies in $C_A$.
  \item \textbf{Construct the source-fixed quotient.} By the image
definition, each $t\in T_{C_A}$ has an anchored preimage $a\in C_A$.
For every anchored patch $U$, extend $a$ to $E$ as the same matching
and restrict it to $U$.  The result belongs to
$\mathscr F^{C_A}(U)$ and reads $t$.  Thus the record map is
sectionwise surjective and hence a regular epimorphism of sheaves.
Apply the regular-epi pullback argument of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-modal-descent}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent Certified histories are a pullback of the retained anchor
predicate, not an unrestricted intersection of predicates on partial
matchings.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathscr F^{C_A}\arrow[r,hook]\arrow[d]
 &\mathscr F\arrow[d,"(-)|_A"]\\
 \underline{C_A}\arrow[r,hook]&\underline{\mathscr F(A)}
 \arrow[ul,phantom,"\lrcorner",very near start]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{theorem}[Completed, authorized and world-indexed witness recovery]
\label{thm:sheaf-finite-protocol-completion}
For the finite causal protocol of
Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-finite-protocol},
$\mathscr F=\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}$ is a sheaf and
$\Gamma(\mathscr F)\cong\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}$ over
$X=U_{\mathrm{ext}}\times\Sigma$.  Its anchored retained record
has the regular-epimorphism factorization
\[
 q^{\mathrm{fin}}:\mathscr F\twoheadrightarrow
 \underline{T_{\mathrm{fin}}},\qquad
 T_{\mathrm{fin}}=
 \operatorname{im}(d_A|_{\mathscr F(A)}).
\]
The accepted and actually authorized subobjects
$\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{acc}}$ and $\mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{auth}}$
constructed above are sheaves.  Their global sections are exactly
the completed histories satisfying, respectively, the protocol's
acceptance test and that test together with its issuer-token witness.
Each has a regular-epimorphism retained-record quotient onto the
image of its anchored record map, with the exact source-fixed modal
comparisons of Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-modal-descent}.

For a situated world carrier $W$ and its external-input map
$u:W\to U_{\mathrm{ext}}$, write
$X_W=W\times\Sigma$ and
$\alpha=u\times\id_\Sigma:X_W\to X$.  There is a cartesian
reconstruction
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-world-completed-pullback}
 \mathscr F_W=\underline{X_W}\times_{\underline X}\mathscr F,
 \qquad
 \Gamma(\mathscr F_W)\cong
 X_W\times_X\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}=\Xi_W.
\end{equation}
Writing $T_W=X_W\times_XT_{\mathrm{fin}}$, the induced map
\[
 q_W:\mathscr F_W\twoheadrightarrow\underline{T_W}
\]
is a regular epimorphism.  All these comparisons commute with
further world substitution and with the accepted and authorized
pullbacks.  The original witnessed epistemic action-event carrier and its
updated-observation kernels are recovered by the canonical
regular-epimorphism comparison of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-updated-action-comparison}, constructed from
the record images of
Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data}.
The set of policies having a completed or authorized witness remains
the image of the corresponding witness-to-policy projection.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Reconstruct the completed histories.} Each matching
of $\iota_x:Q_x\hookrightarrow E$ with itself is the diagonal of
a configuration of $Q_x$, since tagged labels are injective.  Its
secured order is the original causal order.  The final-report
predicate is determined by restriction to $A$, so compatible
completed local histories have the uniquely completed amalgamation
of Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-secured-gluing}.  At the terminal patch,
these are precisely the previously constructed $\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}$,
including their reference and owner-profile projections.
  \item \textbf{Derive acceptance and authorization.} The causal-height
recursion of Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-causal-protocol} constructs the
completed terminal outcome $z_X(x)$ from the full parameter $x$.
Hence its acceptance predicate is the inverse image of $X_Q$ under
the persistent parameter map, and the accepted sheaf is a pullback
as displayed in Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-finite-protocol}.
The matched issuer and recipient occurrences are all retained in $A$.
The incidence image \eqref{eq:sheaf-token-incidence} is true exactly
when each required token role has a matched synchronization in the
completed history.  Consequently the global token predicate is the
inverse image of $C_A$ along $\rho_A$, and it equalizes the kernel
pair of $\rho_A$.  Proposition~\ref{prop:sheaf-certificate-descent} proves
that their intersection is a sheaf with exactly the accepted,
issuer-certified completed global sections.  Neither predicate
follows from the bare token type.
  \item \textbf{Recover completed record quotients.} Every record in
the image of the anchored completed, accepted or authorized
readout has a completing anchored preimage.  Extend its matching
graph to the full interface and restrict to any anchored patch.
The completion, acceptance parameter, and issuer certificate are
preserved.  The resulting record morphisms are sectionwise
surjective and therefore regular epimorphisms, as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:sheaf-retained-surjection} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:sheaf-certificate-descent}.  Their
source-fixed relation lifting is Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-modal-descent}.
  \item \textbf{Apply cartesian world base change.} The pullback of
Proposition~\ref{prop:sheaf-family-basechange} gives
\eqref{eq:sheaf-world-completed-pullback}, since global sections
preserve that pullback.  The quotient over $\underline X$ pulls
back to $q_W$, which is a regular epimorphism by pullback stability.
Iterated pullback comparisons supply naturality and coherence for
further substitutions.  The same argument applied to the accepted
and authorized subobjects gives their world-indexed forms; no
uncountable event-structure carrier is introduced.
  \item \textbf{Recover enabled action records.} The retained
anchor includes the public final output and the actual recipient
receptions by Construction~\ref{con:sheaf-anchored-observation}.
Hence their joint map on $\Xi_W$ equalizes the kernel pair of
$\Gamma(q_W)$.  Its unique factorization and the regular image
of its world-and-event pairing construct the original enabled
action-event carrier as proved in
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-updated-action-comparison}.  The completed
and authorized policy domains follow by taking the images of their
respective projections to $\Sigma$, as in
Construction~\ref{agt-con-protocol-situation}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Canonical action-event image and updated epistemic lifting]
\label{thm:sheaf-updated-action-comparison}
In the world-indexed finite completed protocol of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-finite-protocol-completion}, the earlier
witnessed action-event carrier $U_W$ of
Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data} is the regular
image of a canonically constructed map from $T_W$.  More precisely,
there is a surjection $v_W:T_W\twoheadrightarrow U_W$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-updated-regular-epi}
 Q_W:\mathscr F_W\xrightarrow{q_W}\underline{T_W}
       \xrightarrow{\underline{v_W}}\underline{U_W}
\end{equation}
is a regular epimorphism of sheaves.  If
$o_i^+:U_W\to O_i\times V_i$ is the already constructed updated
observation, put $\beta_i=o_i^+v_W$.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-updated-kernel}
 \kerpair(\beta_i)
 =(v_W\times v_W)^*\kerpair(o_i^+).
\end{equation}
For every relation $R\hookrightarrow U_W^2$, including the
individual and distributed updated observation relations, the
source-fixed lift along $Q_W$ is a regular epimorphism, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sheaf-updated-modal}
 Q_W^*[R]P=[(Q_W\times Q_W)^*R]Q_W^*P,
 \qquad
 Q_W^*\langle R\rangle P
   =\langle(Q_W\times Q_W)^*R\rangle Q_W^*P.
\end{equation}
These comparisons preserve the finite-path common-knowledge relation,
and are coherent under world substitution.  The same construction
applies to the completed accepted and issuer-authorized subcarriers,
using their corresponding regular images.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Descend the delivered-record map.} Let
$\rho_W=\Gamma(q_W):\Xi_W\twoheadrightarrow T_W$.
Its surjectivity follows from the explicit extension of a completed
anchored matching to the full interface.  Let
\[
 \widetilde d_W=\langle d_0,(d_i)_{i\in N}\rangle:
 \Xi_W\longrightarrow V_0\times\prod_iV_i
\]
be the existing joint delivered-record map.  The readout
$d_A$ explicitly retains its public and recipient restrictions, so
$\widetilde d_W$ equalizes the kernel pair of $\rho_W$.  By
effective descent in $\mathbf{Set}$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-kernel-descent}), there is a unique map
$\bar d_W:T_W\to V_0\times\prod_iV_i$ with
$\widetilde d_W=\bar d_W\rho_W$.
  \item \textbf{Construct the original action-event image.} Factor
$\bar d_W$ by regular image,
\[
 T_W\xrightarrow{e_W}E_W
 \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow V_0\times\prod_iV_i.
\]
Since $\rho_W$ is surjective,
$E_W=\operatorname{im}(\widetilde d_W)$, exactly the event carrier
of Construction~\ref{agt-con-witnessed-action-data}.  Let
$w_T:T_W\to W$ be the source-world projection, and form
$\langle w_T,e_W\rangle:T_W\to W\times E_W$.
Its image equals the image of
$\langle w_T,e_W\rangle\rho_W$, hence the previously constructed
enabling subobject
\[
 U_W=\operatorname{im}\langle s,q\rangle
 \hookrightarrow W\times E_W.
\]
Corestriction to that image constructs the surjection
$v_W:T_W\twoheadrightarrow U_W$.  The constant presheaf on the
nonempty-cover site is a sheaf, so $\underline{v_W}$ is
sectionwise surjective and therefore a regular epimorphism.
Composing with $q_W$ proves \eqref{eq:sheaf-updated-regular-epi}.
  \item \textbf{Recover the exact updated observation.} Define
$\beta_i=o_i^+v_W$, where
$o_i^+(w,e)=(o_i(w),b_i(e))$ is the original world-and-receipt
observation. Here $b_i$ already includes the actual public receipt
when public delivery is specified; for the canonical protocol its
three-coordinate form is
Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-public-delivered-observation}.
Functoriality of kernel pairs under inverse image
gives \eqref{eq:sheaf-updated-kernel}.  Pullback preserves finite
intersections, so the same equality holds for distributed knowledge.
No original private observation is inferred solely from an event
record.
  \item \textbf{Lift every alternative at its specified source.} For
$R\hookrightarrow U_W^2$ put
$\widetilde R=(Q_W\times Q_W)^*\underline R$.  The comparison
\[
 \widetilde R\longrightarrow
 \mathscr F_W\times_{\underline{U_W},p_1}\underline R
\]
is the base change of the regular epimorphism $Q_W$ along the
target leg $p_2$.  It is therefore a regular epimorphism and
preserves the given source witness.  Beck--Chevalley and the
quantifier equations of Theorem~\ref{thm:sheaf-modal-descent}
prove \eqref{eq:sheaf-updated-modal}.  For a finite path of
updated epistemic steps, lift successive edges at their prescribed
sources; conversely every lifted path projects.  This establishes
the common-knowledge comparison.  Corollary~\ref{cor:sheaf-modal-fixed-point}
then transports the corresponding positive fixed-point tests.
  \item \textbf{Prove cartesian substitution and authorization.} For
$t:W'\to W$, the completed-witness and retained-record families
are pullbacks by \eqref{eq:sheaf-world-completed-pullback}.  The
surjective image $\langle s,q\rangle$ is stable under these
cartesian pullbacks, so the enabled pair carrier satisfies the
canonical identification $U_{W'}\cong W'\times_WU_W$ inside
$W'\times E_W$.  The separately constructed event-image carrier
$E_{W'}$ may be a subobject of $E_W$; the enabling image is
unchanged under that identification.  Uniqueness of regular-image
factorizations makes $v_{W'}$ the pullback of $v_W$ up to this
canonical comparison, and successive substitutions give the same
identifications.  Updated observations commute because
$o_i'(w')=o_i(tw')$.  Repeating the image construction on accepted
or issuer-authorized completed histories proves the final assertion;
the accepted and token predicates were already shown to be anchored
pullbacks in Proposition~\ref{prop:sheaf-certificate-descent}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent The action-event enabling image is recovered from the
retained completed witness record, without a separately stipulated
epistemic relation.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathscr F_W\arrow[r,two heads,"q_W"]\arrow[dr, two heads,"Q_W"']
   &\underline{T_W}\arrow[d,two heads,"\underline{v_W}"]\\
 &\underline{U_W}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\noindent The world-indexed witness and retained-record maps are
cartesian reindexings of the finite-input family.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathscr F_W\arrow[r,"q_W",two heads]\arrow[d]
 &\underline{T_W}\arrow[d]\\
 \mathscr F\arrow[r,"q^{\mathrm{fin}}"',two heads]
 &\underline{T_{\mathrm{fin}}}
 \arrow[ul,phantom,"\lrcorner",very near start]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\noindent Completion is a predicate on retained causal evidence, rather
than a consequence of finding an arbitrary partial matching.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathscr K_A^{\mathrm{fin}}\arrow[r,hook]\arrow[d,two heads,"q^{\mathrm{fin}}"']
   &\mathscr K_A\arrow[d,two heads,"q"]\\
 \underline{T_{\mathrm{fin}}}\arrow[r,hook]&\underline T
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{remark}[Independent proof-relevant certificates]
An independently exhibited certificate carrier is not identified with
an issuer-produced token.  For an existing certificate map
$c:K\to W_{\mathrm{prot}}$ and the existing completed-state map
$v:\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}\to W_{\mathrm{prot}}$, form the pullback
$K_{\mathrm{exec}}=K\times_{W_{\mathrm{prot}}}\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}$.
Its projection to $\Xi_{\mathrm{in}}\cong\Gamma(\mathscr F)$
transposes under $\underline{(-)}\dashv\Gamma$ to the sheaf map
\[
 \underline{K_{\mathrm{exec}}}\longrightarrow\mathscr F.
\]
This preserves distinct certificate--execution pairs and their
ordinary policy projections.  A certificate which identifies only a
protocol state does not, by itself, identify a unique issuer event.
If a certificate predicate is specified directly on global completed
histories, Proposition~\ref{prop:sheaf-certificate-descent} gives its
exact anchor-descent test.  Taking the full interface as anchor
always represents such a predicate, but need not retain a nontrivial
localization.  These are constructed comparisons of the existing
certificate carrier, not additional certificate axioms.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The completed boundary and finite termination]
For finite causal decision protocols with the designated completed
report, Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-causal-protocol} computes the finished
action assignment for each external input and complete policy.
Authorization is a separate witnessed predicate and may hold for only
some of those profiles.  In other witnessed interactions a completion
fibre may be empty; all the descent and lifting results then apply on
the \emph{image} of the completed-witness projection, not on
unimplemented alternatives.  The outcome and charge of a completed
execution still descend to a coarser policy quotient exactly under the
kernel-pair test of Proposition~\ref{prop:measured-comparison-descent}.
\end{remark}


\section{Strategic Communication and the Creation of Knowledge}\label{sec:paper-11}

Communication can give several agents information that none possessed alone. In the
two-bit institution, each owner first sees a private bit. The collector already
holds the pair before either recipient has necessarily received it. We therefore
evaluate what the recipients know at the completed-delivery boundary. The image of
the completed execution map gives the event carrier, and each recipient's projection
gives its observation. To compare strategic alternatives, we also keep the complete
policy behind each current message. The split-surjection and lifting results specify
which claims about choice and knowledge can then be read from the public messages.

\subsection{Public inspection and the disclosure of pooled information}
\label{sec:egt-public-inspection}

The image in Construction~\ref{con:egt-pooled-observation} is a joint
signal. Disclosing its value is an epistemic action that can be described
simultaneously at every reference state. For observation relations
$R_i=\ker(o_i)$ on $W$ and a coalition $C$, write
\[
 R_C=\bigcap_{i\in C}R_i,\qquad
 \mathsf{DK}_C(P)=[R_C]P,\qquad
 \mathsf{CK}_C(P)=\left[\left(\bigcup_{i\in C}R_i\right)^*\right]P.
\]
The first predicate is distributed knowledge. The second is common
knowledge within $C$; for $C=N$ it is the previously defined
$\mathsf{CK}$. Empty intersection is $W^2$, while the reflexive
transitive closure of the empty union is equality. These conventions
also define both operations for the empty coalition.

\begin{construction}[Public inspection of a signal]
\label{con:egt-public-inspection}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Construct the inspection update.} For $q:W\to O$, let $E=\operatorname{im}(q)$, enable precisely the pair
$(w,q(w))$, and equip every agent's action set with equality. The
updated carrier is canonically $W$ and
\[
 R_i^q=R_i\cap\ker(q).
\]
If $R_i=\ker(o_i)$, the updated observation is
$\langle o_i,q\rangle$.
  \item \textbf{Restrict to the designated signal fibre.} At a designated world $w$, the component
$q^{-1}(q(w))$ is the announcement of the observed value. This fibre is closed under all
updated accessibility relations. Its inclusion is bounded, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-modal-adequacy} identifies its modal interpretation
with that of the full-carrier update at $w$.
Retaining every possible outcome at once gives the full-carrier
presentation of public inspection
\citep{VanEijckGattingerWang2017KnowingValues}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{proposition}[Inspection is an idempotent coreflection]
\label{prop:egt-inspection-coreflection}
In the poset of relation families on a fixed carrier $W$, ordered by
componentwise inclusion, let $\mathcal R_q$ be the subposet with
$T_i\subseteq\ker(q)$ for every $i$. Its inclusion $\iota$ has
right adjoint
\[
 \mathsf{Inspect}_q(R)_i=R_i\cap\ker(q),
 \qquad\iota\dashv\mathsf{Inspect}_q.
\]
Write $\mathsf I_q=\iota\mathsf{Inspect}_q$ for the associated
idempotent comonad on the full relation poset. For two fixed signals
$q,r$ on $W$, these endofunctors satisfy
\[
 \mathsf I_r\mathsf I_q
 =\mathsf I_{\langle q,r\rangle}
 =\mathsf I_q\mathsf I_r.
\]
These statements also hold in the poset of S5 relation families.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Adjunction and transposition.} For $T\in\mathcal R_q$, $T\subseteq R$ if and only if
$T\subseteq R\cap\ker(q)$. This is the adjunction. Its associated endofunctor $\mathsf I_q$ has counit
$R\cap\ker(q)\subseteq R$ and is idempotent.
  \item \textbf{Predicate calculation.} The composition law follows from
$\ker\langle q,r\rangle=\ker(q)\cap\ker(r)$. Meets preserve
equivalence relations, proving the S5 version.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Public pooling turns distributed knowledge into common knowledge]
\label{thm:egt-public-pooling}
Let $R_i=\ker(o_i)$ and let $C\subseteq N$ be nonempty. Form the
image factorization of the tuple of coalition observations,
\[
 W\xrightarrow{q_C}O_C\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
 \prod_{i\in C}O_i,
 \qquad R_C=\ker(q_C)=\bigcap_{i\in C}R_i.
\]
After public inspection of $q_C$, the common-knowledge relation of all
owners is exactly $R_C$. Consequently, for every fixed factual predicate
$A\subseteq W$,
\[
 \mathsf{CK}_N^{\,q_C}(A)=\mathsf{DK}_C(A),\qquad
 \mathsf{DK}_C(A):=[R_C]A.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Predicate calculation.} Each updated relation is $R_i^+=R_i\cap R_C$. If $i\in C$ this
is $R_C$; for other $i$ it is contained in $R_C$. Since $C$ is nonempty,
\[
 \bigcup_{i\in N}R_i^+=R_C.
\]
The relation $R_C$ is an equivalence relation, hence equals its own
reflexive transitive closure. Taking relational boxes proves the equation.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Private pooling within a coalition]
\label{cor:egt-private-pooling}
Use the same event set and enabling relation, but take $S_i$ to be
equality for $i\in C$ and the universal relation for $i\notin C$.
Then members have updated relation $R_C$ and outsiders retain $R_i$.
For fixed $A$, common knowledge within $C$ after this update equals
$\mathsf{DK}_C(A)$ before it.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Ownerwise alternatives.} Product update intersects member relations with $\ker(q_C)$ and leaves
outsider relations unchanged. The union of the member relations is $R_C$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

This private construction is the resolution of distributed knowledge studied
by \citet{AgotnesWang2016ResolvingDistributedKnowledge}.
Public inspection additionally
reveals the pooled value to outsiders. In both equations $A$ is retained as a
fixed subobject. An epistemic formula re-evaluated after the update may
denote a different subobject; Remark~\ref{rem:egt-announcement-reevaluation} makes this explicit.

\begin{proposition}[A connectivity obstruction for general signals]
\label{prop:egt-inspection-connectivity}
Let $E=(\bigcup_iR_i)^*$ and
$E^q=(\bigcup_i(R_i\cap\ker(q)))^*$. Then
\[
 E^q\subseteq E\cap\ker(q).
\]
For the quotient $c:W\to W/E$, there is a canonical surjection
\[
 W/E^q\longrightarrow\operatorname{im}\langle c,q\rangle.
\]
It is an isomorphism exactly when every nonempty intersection of an
$E$-class with a $q$-fibre is connected by the original $R_i$-edges
that stay inside that intersection.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Lifting along the surjection.} Every generating updated edge preserves both the $E$-class and $q$. Thus both are constant on $E^q$-classes. This gives the factor map,
which is surjective because its target is the image.
  \item \textbf{Injectivity of the event quotient.} It is injective
exactly when equality of those two retained values implies $E^q$
relatedness. The definition of reflexive transitive closure identifies
this with the stated connectivity condition.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{example}
On $W=\{a,b,c\}$ let $R_1$ have classes $\{a,b\},\{c\}$ and
$R_2$ have classes $\{a\},\{b,c\}$. Put $q(a)=q(c)=0$ and
$q(b)=1$. Then $E=W^2$, but every updated individual relation is
equality. Hence $E^q$ is equality, whereas $E\cap\ker(q)$ still
relates $a$ to $c$. Common knowledge cannot generally be updated by
intersecting the old common-knowledge relation with the signal kernel.
\end{example}

\begin{construction}[Finite operational disclosure]
\label{con:egt-finite-disclosure}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Collect the observed tuple.} For the observation maps $o_i:W\to O_i$, take their image
factorizations $W\twoheadrightarrow F_i\hookrightarrow O_i$.
When these images are finite and $C$ is nonempty, the collector and
iterated data comultiplication form the strategy
\[
 \bigotimes_{i\in C}D(F_i)
 \xrightarrow{c_C}D\!\left(\prod_{i\in C}F_i\right)
 \xrightarrow{\Delta^{(N)}}
 \bigotimes_{j\in N}D\!\left(\prod_{i\in C}F_i\right).
\]
The collector law of Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-finite-collectors}
sends the supplied value states to their tuple state.
  \item \textbf{Deliver the tuple.} The comonoid law
of Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-data-comonoid} places that tuple at every
recipient's output. Equality of tuples has kernel $R_C$, so this realizes
the disclosed signal of Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-public-pooling} on the
supplied observation values.
  \item \textbf{Update the recipient observations.} Retaining each recipient's old observation
gives the updated map $\langle o_j,q_C\rangle$.
The collector waits for all coalition inputs; a decision that uses the
disclosure is wired after the corresponding output occurrence.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

The signal map identifies the information to be disclosed. The strategy exhibits the
collecting and delivery events for those signals. A decision downstream can depend
on the disclosure once the relevant delivery has occurred.

\subsection{Agent-labelled truthful public actions}

\begin{construction}[The public announcement performed by an agent]
\label{con:egt-agent-authored-announcement}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Form the authored action interface.} Fix an observed agent presentation on $W$, with effective quotients
$\bar o_j:W\twoheadrightarrow\Omega_j$. For a sender $i$, take the action
set $E_i=\mathcal P(\Omega_i)$ and enable $B\in E_i$ at $w$ precisely when
$\bar o_i(w)\in B$. Every observer's action relation is equality on $E_i$.
  \item \textbf{Compute its content.} The content and updated carrier are
\[
 A_{i,B}=\bar o_i^{-1}(B),\qquad
 \mathcal U_i=\{(w,B):w\in A_{i,B}\}.
\]
The sender identity is part of the action interface.
  \item \textbf{Interpret the pointed announcement.} Write
$\mathsf{say}_i(B)$ for the corresponding pointed public action. If
$a_{i,B}:A_{i,B}\hookrightarrow W$ and
$j_{i,B}:A_{i,B}\to\mathcal U_i$ are the inclusion and
$w\mapsto(w,B)$, its modalities are
\[
 [\mathsf{say}_i(B)]Q=\forall_{a_{i,B}}j_{i,B}^*Q,
 \qquad
 \langle\mathsf{say}_i(B)\rangle Q=\exists_{a_{i,B}}j_{i,B}^*Q.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{proposition}[Authored announcement and public restriction]
\label{prop:egt-agent-announcement-restriction}
The content $A_{i,B}$ is invariant under the sender's observation relation,
so $K_iA_{i,B}=A_{i,B}$. The component of $\mathcal U_i$ at event $B$ is
isomorphic as an observed frame to $M|_{A_{i,B}}$. Consequently an
agent-labelled announcement has exactly the public-restriction semantics of
its content, with epistemic formulas evaluated in that restricted frame.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} If $\bar o_i(v)=\bar o_i(w)$, membership of that common value in $B$ is the
same at $v$ and $w$. This proves observation invariance and the knowledge
equation. The product-update relation at $B$ is
\[
 (w,B)R_j^+(v,B)
 \iff wR_jv\ \text{and}\ w,v\in A_{i,B},
\]
because the action relation is equality.
  \item \textbf{Isomorphism of restricted action models.} Thus $w\mapsto(w,B)$ is a frame
isomorphism from the restriction onto that component, preserving the
restricted factual terms. The displayed dynamic modalities are precisely
the inclusion quantifiers of the public restriction. Frame isomorphism and
the defining logical operations give the assertion for re-evaluated
epistemic formulas and their fixed points.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

This realizes a sender-labelled public test for the
observation-invariant message family. Joint communication consists of
one such component per owner, but its strategic interpretation requires
complete policies specifying messages at every observation. We
construct those carriers next.

\begin{construction}[A public test as an institutional agent action]
\label{con:egt-institutional-public-test}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Supply the test and its owner.} For any predicate $P\hookrightarrow W$, form its characteristic term
$\chi_P:W\to2$ in the paper's ordinary base and corestrict it to
$\Omega_P=\operatorname{im}(\chi_P)$. Extend the owner list by a fresh
institutional identity $\ast$, retaining all original world observations.
Give this agent observation $\chi_P:W\twoheadrightarrow\Omega_P$ and the
truthful message interface $\mathcal P(\Omega_P)$.
  \item \textbf{Realize the truthful disclosure.} The complete policy
$\eta_P(o)=\{o\}$ discloses the test result. Its successful public event is
$B_P=\Omega_P\cap\{1\}$; if $P$ is empty, that event has empty enabling
carrier. The original agents publicly receive the disclosed result.
  \item \textbf{Factor the implementation.} The ordinary test and its concurrent realization have distinct types:
\[
 W\xrightarrow{\chi_P}2,
 \qquad
 D(\Omega_P)\xrightarrow{\widehat{\chi}}D(2)
 \xrightarrow{\text{success gate}}D(1),
\]
where $\chi:\Omega_P\to2$ is the inclusion of the image of $\chi_P$.
The first arrow is the \emph{specified ordinary signal input} and not
an event-structure sensor inferred from an arbitrary predicate on $W$.
The data strategy implements the second, finite-stage operation after
that input is actually supplied.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{proposition}[Public comprehension realized by a test agent]
\label{prop:egt-institutional-public-test}
The successful branch of this institutional action has enabling carrier
$P$, and its frame on the original agent indices is exactly $M|_P$.
Its dynamic modalities on retained predicates are the paper's public
restriction modalities. The disclosure component has a finite concurrent
realization, with its input supplied by the ordinary term $\chi_P$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Policy-level comparison.} The event $B_P$ is enabled precisely when
$\chi_P(w)\in\Omega_P\cap\{1\}$, equivalently $w\in P$. At such a
world the complete policy $\eta_P$ outputs exactly $B_P=\{1\}$; if no
such world exists both enabling carriers are empty. Equality of public
events restricts each original relation $R_j$ to $P\times P$.
  \item \textbf{Predicate calculation.} Projection
of the successful component to $P$ is therefore a frame isomorphism for
those indices and the retained factual terms. Its inclusion into $W$ is
the same comprehension map, proving both dynamic quantifier equations.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} The observation image has at most two elements. Its singleton response and
public broadcast are the finite data constructions of the operational
semantics. The term $\chi_P$ supplies their ordinary reference input; the
implementation realizes the finite disclosure interface.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge: completion.} Predicate
evaluation remains the ordinary semantic test that constructed $\chi_P$. The original agents' pre-action observations are retained, and the extra
institutional observation is explicitly part of this extended presentation.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


The implementation records who sends the test, which result is
delivered, and which event succeeds. Thus the logical update has an
observable cause rather than an unexplained restriction of worlds.
The finite disclosure protocol acts on the test-result interface; the
underlying world remains an ordinary parameter.

\subsection{The full truthful message family and coalition announcement games}
\label{sec:egt-coalition-announcements}

A truthful public message is controlled by its sender, but its
content is constrained by that sender's observation. Power objects and
comprehension generate the entire semantic family of such messages.
The coalition effectivity quantifiers then test whether a group can
secure a post-announcement goal against truthful outsiders. This
relates strategic control of disclosure to the joint-signal operation
of Section~\ref{sec:egt-public-inspection}.

\begin{construction}[Truthful message families]
\label{con:egt-announcement-game}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Form the observed message carriers.} Let $M=(W,(\ker(o_i))_{i\in N})$. Factor each observation as
$W\xrightarrow{\bar o_i}\Omega_i\hookrightarrow O_i$, where
$\Omega_i=\operatorname{im}(o_i)$. Define the ordinary message object
$\mathsf{Msg}_i=\mathcal P(\Omega_i)$ and its admissible fibre
\[
 \mathsf{Msg}_i(w)=\{B_i\subseteq\Omega_i:\bar o_i(w)\in B_i\}.
\]
  \item \textbf{Interpret message contents.} The message $B_i$ announces the predicate
$A_i=\bar o_i^{-1}(B_i)$. This predicate is observation-invariant;
when $B_i$ is admissible at $w$, $K_iA_i(w)$ holds. Conversely every
observation-invariant predicate is the inverse image of a unique subset
of $\Omega_i$, by Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-predicate-descent}.
  \item \textbf{Construct the updated model.} For $\mathsf{Msg}=\prod_i\mathsf{Msg}_i$ and $B\in\mathsf{Msg}$, put
\[
 A_B=\bigcap_i\bar o_i^{-1}(B_i),\qquad M_B=M|_{A_B}.
\]
The updated carriers form the ordinary dependent family
$\pi:\mathcal U=\{(B,v):v\in A_B\}\to\mathsf{Msg}$.
Its $i$-relation relates $(B,v)$ and $(B',v')$ precisely when
$B=B'$ and $v\ker(o_i)v'$. Thus all epistemic operations in a fibre
are those of $M_B$.
  \item \textbf{Specify goals and legal messages.} A goal is a specified subobject
$\Psi\hookrightarrow\mathcal U$.

The legal message family over the reference state is
\[
 L=\{(w,B):B_i\in\mathsf{Msg}_i(w)\text{ for all }i\}
 \longrightarrow W.
\]
For $C\subseteq N$, let
$L_C=\{(w,B_C):B_i\in\mathsf{Msg}_i(w)\ (i\in C)\}$,
and write $e_C:L\to L_C$ and $u_C:L_C\to W$ for the projections.
These are the realizable coalition-coordinate objects in each fibre:
every partial tuple has the canonical completion $B_j=\Omega_j$ for
$j\notin C$. The map $g:L\to\mathcal U$, $(w,B)\mapsto(B,w)$,
evaluates the goal in the announced context. Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:egt-announcement-ability}
 \mathsf{AnnAbility}_C(\Psi)
 =\exists_{u_C}\,\forall_{e_C}\,g^*\Psi
 \quad\in\mathsf{Pred}(W).
\end{equation}
In particular, at $w$ this asserts that some truthful coalition message
tuple succeeds against every simultaneous truthful outsider tuple.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

The construction uses power objects, products, projection, and
comprehension. Equation~\eqref{eq:egt-announcement-ability} is the
fibrewise instance of Equation~\eqref{eq:egt-legal-ability}; its
quantifiers follow the coalition-announcement pattern. Standard
announcement logics restrict messages to a specified epistemic syntax
\citep{AgotnesEtAl2010GroupAnnouncements,
GalimullinAlechina2018CoalitionGroupAnnouncement}; our full semantic
family instead contains all observation-invariant subobjects. Group
announcement logics with distributed knowledge are discussed by
\citet{AgotnesEtAl2022GroupDistributed}. The results below state their
own factual-goal and full-family scope rather than identifying these
different languages.

\begin{theorem}[Exact announcement ability for factual common knowledge]
\label{thm:egt-coalition-announcement}
For $P\subseteq W$, let $P^+=\{(B,v)\in\mathcal U:v\in P\}$
and take $\Psi_P=\mathsf{CK}_N^{\mathcal U}(P^+)$, using the
fibre-preserving relations of Construction~\ref{con:egt-announcement-game}.
For every nonempty coalition $C$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:egt-announcement-distributed-knowledge}
 \mathsf{AnnAbility}_C(\Psi_P)=\mathsf{DK}_C(P).
\end{equation}
The sufficient coalition policy is the uniform observation-admissible
map $o\mapsto\{o\}$ for each member. For $C=\varnothing$,
$\mathsf{AnnAbility}_{\varnothing}(\Psi_P)=\mathsf{CK}_N^M(P)$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent A truthful announcement is represented as an informed section over the observation quotient.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
W\arrow[r,"o_C",two heads]\arrow[d,"m"']
 &O_C\arrow[d,"\pi"]\\
 M\arrow[r,equal]&M
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}


\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At $w\in\mathsf{DK}_C(P)$, let every member announce
$B_i=\{\bar o_i(w)\}$. For every admissible outsider tuple,
\[
 w\in A_B\subseteq R_C[w]\subseteq P.
\]
The fact therefore holds throughout the updated carrier and is common
knowledge there. Each chosen message is a function of the owner's
observation alone, proving uniform observation-admissibility by
Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-observation}.
  \item \textbf{Reverse implication.} Conversely, let a coalition tuple establish the displayed common knowledge
against every outsider tuple. Take $B_j=\Omega_j$ for outsiders. Truthfulness and observation invariance give $R_C[w]\subseteq A_B$.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} For any $i\in C$, each $v\in R_C[w]$ is $R_i$-accessible from $w$
inside $A_B$. Common knowledge in this updated model therefore gives
$v\in P$. This is $\mathsf{DK}_C(P)(w)$.
  \item \textbf{Ownerwise alternatives.} For the empty coalition, the outsider tuple of all tautological messages
leaves the original model unchanged, proving necessity.
  \item \textbf{Reverse implication.} Conversely every
path in a restriction containing $w$ is an original path. Hence common
knowledge of the fixed fact is preserved under all these restrictions. For $N=\varnothing$, the common-knowledge relation is equality and the
same argument gives the predicate $P$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


\begin{proposition}[Finite message realizations]
\label{prop:egt-finite-announcement-messages}
When all observation images $\Omega_i$ are finite, the full message
objects, singleton disclosure maps, and truthfulness tests in
Construction~\ref{con:egt-announcement-game} have finite data realizations.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Message-policy and membership protocols.} Each $\mathcal P(\Omega_i)$ is finite. The map
$\Omega_i\to\mathcal P(\Omega_i)$, $o\mapsto\{o\}$, and the
membership function $\Omega_i\times\mathcal P(\Omega_i)\to2$
have response strategies by Proposition~\ref{prop:egt-functions}. Collectors form joint messages, and the data comonoids broadcast them.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} The public enabling subobject is the conjunction of the membership tests,
so its finite presentation is
Construction~\ref{con:egt-finite-action-enablement} on these signal and
message carriers. Observational distinctions on an arbitrary original
state carrier remain in the ordinary dependent family over that carrier.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

The construction specifies a full semantic message family. A chosen
communication language is represented by its own message object and
content map; its effectivity is then obtained by the same dependent
quantifiers. The equality in
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-coalition-announcement} is established for the
constructed full family, whose singleton policy is explicitly available.

\subsection{Complete truthful policies of communicating agents}
\label{sec:egt-complete-announcement-policies}

The message actually sent fixes only one entry of an announcement policy. To ask
what the sender could have disclosed at another observation, we retain the entire
policy. This follows the contingent announcements of
\citet{AgotnesVanDitmarsch2011AnnouncementGames}. For the observation-invariant
message family constructed above, we compare complete truthful policies with their
current public messages and keep both the private policy records and the execution
witnesses. The comparison concerns this qualitative family. A restricted message
language changes the available responses.

\begin{construction}[The complete truthful announcement interface]
\label{con:egt-complete-announcement-policies}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Form complete truthful policies.} Use the effective observation images and message carriers of
Construction~\ref{con:egt-announcement-game}. Define
\[
 \mathsf{AnnPol}_i
 =\prod_{o\in\Omega_i}\{B\subseteq\Omega_i:o\in B\},
 \qquad
 \mathsf{AnnPol}=\prod_{i\in N}\mathsf{AnnPol}_i.
\]
A policy $\pi_i$ is a truthful message response at every possible
observation, including observations different from the current one.
It is an ordinary subobject of $\mathsf{Msg}_i^{\Omega_i}$.
  \item \textbf{Evaluate at the current observation.} Its evaluation is
\[
 e_i:\Omega_i\times\mathsf{AnnPol}_i\to\mathsf{Msg}_i,
 \qquad e_i(o,\pi_i)=\pi_i(o).
\]
At $w$, the legal output of the agent is $\pi_i(\bar o_i(w))$.
The agent's policy carrier is $\mathsf{AnnPol}_i$, with its canonical
selection interface; a goal or comparison is connected to the resulting
message or updated state as in the preceding agent calculus.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{lemma}[Explicit extension of a truthful message]
\label{lem:egt-truthful-policy-extension}
\label{agt-lem-message-extension}
For every $o\in\Omega_i$, the evaluation map
\[
 e_{i,o}:\mathsf{AnnPol}_i\twoheadrightarrow
        \{B\subseteq\Omega_i:o\in B\}
\]
has the explicit section $B\mapsto E_{i,B}$, where
\[
 E_{i,B}(x)=B\cup\{x\}.
\]
In particular every legal message at $w$ is the current output of an
exhibited complete truthful policy.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Split evaluation of public messages.} Every value of $E_{i,B}$ contains $x$, so the function belongs to
$\mathsf{AnnPol}_i$. Since $o\in B$, evaluation at $o$ is
$E_{i,B}(o)=B\cup\{o\}=B$. Hence $e_{i,o}(E_{i,B})=B$. The formula is defined
for every indicated pair and uses no choice of a representative.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent Truthful messages extend to complete policies that evaluate to the chosen message at the given observation.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
\{B\subseteq\Omega_i:o\in B\}\arrow[r,"E_{i,-}"]\arrow[dr,"\id"']
 &\AnnPol_i\arrow[d,"e_{i,o}",two heads]\\
 &\{B\subseteq\Omega_i:o\in B\}
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{construction}[The policy-state model of public communication]
\label{con:egt-announcement-policy-model}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Form policy states and their message map.} Put $\mathcal X=W\times\mathsf{AnnPol}$ and define the joint evaluation
\[
 b(w,\pi)=(\pi_i(\bar o_i(w)))_{i\in N}.
\]
The map to the paper's public-message carrier, retaining its original
coordinate order, is
\[
 F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal U,
 \qquad F(w,\pi)=(b(w,\pi),w).
\]
  \item \textbf{Update the observations.} Give agent $j$ the pre-communication observation
$\widetilde o_j^0(w,\pi)=(\bar o_j(w),\pi_j)$. Use the public action set
$\mathsf{Msg}$ with equality as every action relation and enabling predicate
$B=b(w,\pi)$. Its updated carrier is canonically $\mathcal X$, since each
source has exactly one enabled joint message. Its post-communication
observation is
\[
 \widetilde o_j(w,\pi)
    =(\bar o_j(w),\pi_j,b(w,\pi)),
 \qquad R_j^{\mathcal X}=\ker(\widetilde o_j).
\]
Thus each agent retains its own complete policy, its original observation,
and the delivered public messages. This is an explicit product-update
instance of the earlier action-model construction.
  \item \textbf{Define strategic alternatives.} The strategic relations hold the reference world fixed:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (w,\pi)D_C^{\mathcal X}(v,\pi')
   &\iff w=v\ \text{and}\ \pi_{-C}=\pi'_{-C},\\
 (B,w)D_C^{\mathcal U}(B',v)
   &\iff w=v\ \text{and}\ B_{-C}=B'_{-C}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The latter are the legal message deviations in each fibre over $W$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[Exact policy-to-message comparison]
\label{thm:egt-announcement-policy-comparison}
\label{agt-thm-message-comparison}
The map $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal U$ is a split surjection and a bounded
morphism for every individual epistemic relation, every nonempty
intersection of those relations, and every coalition-deviation relation.
More explicitly, for $\varnothing\ne J\subseteq N$ it is bounded from
$\bigcap_{j\in J}R_j^{\mathcal X}$ to
$\bigcap_{j\in J}R_j^{\mathcal U}$, and for every $C\subseteq N$ it is
bounded from $D_C^{\mathcal X}$ to $D_C^{\mathcal U}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Ownerwise alternatives.} A section sends $(B,w)\in\mathcal U$ to
\[
 \bigl(w,(E_{i,B_i})_{i\in N}\bigr).
\]
It is well-defined by truthfulness of $B$ at $w$ and is a section by
Lemma~\ref{lem:egt-truthful-policy-extension}. This includes the empty owner
list, when both carriers are canonically $W$.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} Forward preservation of the epistemic relations follows from their
observations: equality of $\widetilde o_j$ implies equality of the original
$j$-observation and of the public tuple. For the back condition, let
$x=(w,\pi)$ and suppose
\[
 F(x)\Bigl(\bigcap_{j\in J}R_j^{\mathcal U}\Bigr)(B,v),
 \qquad J\ne\varnothing.
\]
Then $B=b(w,\pi)$ and $\bar o_j(v)=\bar o_j(w)$ for every $j\in J$.
  \item \textbf{Construction on policy coordinates.} Define a profile at $v$ by
\[
 \pi'_j=\pi_j\quad(j\in J),\qquad
 \pi'_k=E_{k,B_k}\quad(k\notin J).
\]
For a retained coordinate,
$\pi_j(\bar o_j(v))=\pi_j(\bar o_j(w))=B_j$; for every other coordinate
the extension lemma gives the same output. Hence $F(v,\pi')=(B,v)$. For each $j\in J$ the old observation, its own policy, and the public tuple
are unchanged, so $xR_j^{\mathcal X}(v,\pi')$.
  \item \textbf{Lifting intersections along the report map.} This proves the simultaneous
back condition and, in particular, its individual case. For an empty
intersection the universal relation has the same lifting property by
surjectivity alone.
  \item \textbf{Ownerwise alternatives.} For strategic relations, retaining the outsider policies at fixed $w$
retains their evaluated messages, which proves the forward clause. Suppose $F(w,\pi)D_C^{\mathcal U}(B',w)$. Keep
$\pi'_j=\pi_j$ for $j\notin C$ and set
$\pi'_i=E_{i,B'_i}$ for $i\in C$.
  \item \textbf{Ownerwise alternatives: completion.} The outsider outputs are already $B'_{-C}$, and the changed outputs are
$B'_C$ by the extension lemma. Therefore
$F(w,\pi')=(B',w)$ and
$(w,\pi)D_C^{\mathcal X}(w,\pi')$. This proves the back clause for every
coalition, including the empty and grand coalitions.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent The complete-policy comparison is a split surjection with an explicit section.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
\mathcal U\arrow[r,"s"]\arrow[dr,"\id"']
 &\mathcal X\arrow[d,"F",two heads]\\
 &\mathcal U
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{lemma}[Dependent successor-fibre exactness of truthful communication]
\label{lem:egt-announcement-successor-fibres}
For each nonempty observer set $J\subseteq N$, write
$K_J=\bigcap_{j\in J}R_j$ for the joint epistemic relation; for each
coalition $C\subseteq N$, retain $D_C$ for strategic deviations.
For either $R=K_J$ or $R=D_C$, with the corresponding superscripts
$\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal U$, the canonical map of dependent
successor families
\[
 \lambda_R:R^{\mathcal X}\longrightarrow
 \mathcal X\times_{\mathcal U,p_1}R^{\mathcal U},
 \qquad (x,x')\longmapsto(x,(Fx,Fx'))
\]
is surjective. Consequently for every $Q\hookrightarrow\mathcal U$,
\[
 F^*[R^{\mathcal U}]Q=[R^{\mathcal X}]F^*Q,
 \qquad
 F^*\langle R^{\mathcal U}\rangle Q
   =\langle R^{\mathcal X}\rangle F^*Q.
\]
The same statement for an empty epistemic intersection follows from
the split surjection $F$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At a fixed $x\in\mathcal X$, a point of the displayed pullback is a
specified $R^{\mathcal U}$-successor of $Fx$. The epistemic and strategic
back-lifts constructed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-announcement-policy-comparison} provide an
$R^{\mathcal X}$-successor of that very $x$ mapping to it. Thus each
fibre of $\lambda_R$ is inhabited, which is surjectivity in
$\mathbf{Set}$.
  \item \textbf{Predicate calculation.} Forward preservation ensures well-definedness. The source and target existential successor predicates therefore agree on
inverse-image tests. Their universal successor predicates agree as well:
a target test is true on every successor if and only if its pullback is
true on every source successor, because the successor map is onto.
  \item \textbf{Modal preservation for empty coalitions.} This proves both displayed modal equations. For an empty epistemic
intersection the relation is universal; the split surjection supplies
the requisite lift from any fixed source state.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\noindent Alternative lifting is performed over the fixed policy reference.
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
D_C^{\mathcal X}\arrow[r,"\lambda_C",two heads]\arrow[d,"p_1"']
 &\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal U}D_C^{\mathcal U}\arrow[d]\\
 \mathcal X\arrow[r,equal]&\mathcal X
\end{tikzcd}
\end{center}

\begin{corollary}[Knowledge, strategic predicates, and dynamic transport]
\label{cor:egt-announcement-policy-logic}
For predicates and comparisons retained on $\mathcal U$, inverse image
along $F$ preserves the individual knowledge, distributed knowledge,
common-knowledge, coalition-deviation, and positive modal fixed-point
operations. It preserves and reflects validity. For a comparison
$Q_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal U^2$, use
$(F\times F)^*Q_i$ on $\mathcal X^2$. The Nash predicates defined using the
displayed deviation relations satisfy
\[
 \mathsf{NE}_{\mathcal X}=F^*\mathsf{NE}_{\mathcal U},
\]
and the corresponding strict coalitional stability predicates satisfy the
same equality. Public restrictions by retained assertions and action models
pulled back from $\mathcal U$ have the same exact dynamic comparison.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Communication and delivery.} The explicit comparison
$\lambda_R:R^{\mathcal X}\twoheadrightarrow
 \mathcal X\times_{\mathcal U,p_1}R^{\mathcal U}$
of Lemma~\ref{lem:egt-announcement-successor-fibres} gives the two
inverse-image equations
\[
 F^*[R^{\mathcal U}]Q=[R^{\mathcal X}]F^*Q,
 \qquad
 F^*\langle R^{\mathcal U}\rangle Q
    =\langle R^{\mathcal X}\rangle F^*Q.
\]
Here the source reference is not chosen afresh: it is fixed in the
pullback, and every target successor lifts over that same reference.
  \item \textbf{Lifting through the comparison.} Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-modal-adequacy} proves the positive fixed-point
comparison. The intersection lifting in the theorem supplies the distributed
knowledge case directly. Common knowledge uses the same individual
relations and its previously constructed greatest fixed point.
  \item \textbf{Fibrewise calculation.} At a source $x$, every concrete $i$-deviation maps to a target deviation
with comparison $Q_i(Fx,Fx')$, and every target deviation lifts at that same
source. Universal absence of improving alternatives is therefore equivalent
on the two carriers. For a coalition use its lifting clause and the specified
collective comparison; conjunction over coalitions gives the claimed
stability equality.
  \item \textbf{Base-change comparison.} For $V\hookrightarrow\mathcal U$, the restriction
$F^{-1}(V)\to V$ is surjective. A lift of an alternative in $V$ belongs to
$F^{-1}(V)$ by its image, so it remains bounded. Comprehension and
Beck--Chevalley give the public-restriction comparison.
  \item \textbf{Lifting along the surjection.} For a pulled-back
action model apply Corollary~\ref{cor:egt-action-bounded-quotient}. Surjectivity reflects validity in each case.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


The retained language has its predicates on $\mathcal U$, pulled back to
$\mathcal X$. Predicates concerning additional private policy records are
also available on $\mathcal X$ and remain attached to that presentation.
The comparison theorem relates the specified interfaces and their retained
tests; it keeps the whole policy family needed to lift alternatives.

\begin{example}[A public policy record carries additional information]
\label{ex:egt-public-policy-record}
Take two worlds $0,1$. Agent $1$ observes the world, while agent $2$ has one
observation. The truthful policy
$\pi_1(0)=\{0,1\}$, $\pi_1(1)=\{1\}$ sends the tautological message at
$0$. Its content alone leaves both worlds possible to agent $2$. If the
complete policy $\pi_1$ is also publicly delivered, observing that message
identifies world $0$. In the policy-state model of
Construction~\ref{con:egt-announcement-policy-model}, only agent $1$ retains
its own policy as a private record. At world $1$ the alternative policy
$E_{1,\{0,1\}}$ gives the same public message, supplying the lift required
for agent $2$. The example exhibits the informational effect of an additional
policy-record wire and explains the role of the full policy family in $F$.
\end{example}

\subsection{Concurrent implementation and retained policy witnesses}

\begin{proposition}[Concurrent realization of complete announcing agents]
\label{prop:egt-complete-announcement-realization}
\label{agt-prop-ann-implementation}
When the observation images $\Omega_i$ are finite, the complete truthful
policy presentation and its post-communication observations have an
implementation in $\mathbf{DecArena}_N(\mathcal C)$. Its complete owner
policy carriers are $\mathsf{AnnPol}_i$. At reference input
$(\bar o_i(w))_i$ and policy profile $\pi$, its delivered observation to
agent $j$ is
\[
 (\bar o_j(w),\pi_j,b(w,\pi)).
\]
The report decisions are concurrent, and the joint message is delivered
after its component messages are collected.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Realization of announcement policies.} Each $\mathsf{Msg}_i=\mathcal P(\Omega_i)$ and $\mathsf{AnnPol}_i$ is finite. Restrict the decision generator
$\mathsf{Dec}_i(\Omega_i,\mathsf{Msg}_i)$ along the exhibited inclusion
\[
 \mathsf{AnnPol}_i\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Msg}_i^{\Omega_i}.
\]
It realizes policy $\pi_i$ by the response strategy $\widehat{\pi_i}$. Tensor these components and apply the finite collector to their message
outputs.
  \item \textbf{Broadcast of the joint report.} The resulting joint output is $b(w,\pi)$. Broadcast this output
using the iterated data comonoid, one copy for each agent.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} Copy the original input observation to its reporting component and its
owner's retained-observation wire. For a private policy record, use the
singly owned nullary decision generator with response carrier
$\mathsf{AnnPol}_i$; at a fixed policy it realizes the constant
$\ulcorner\pi_i\urcorner:I\to D(\mathsf{AnnPol}_i)$, using the nullary
collector and the response from $1$.
  \item \textbf{Ownerwise alternatives.} Compose these two occurrences of owner
$i$ and reparametrize their product carrier by the diagonal assigning the
same $\pi_i$ to the reporting and record components. This is a permitted
ownerwise reparametrization in the generated calculus. It leaves exactly
$\mathsf{AnnPol}_i$ as the complete policy carrier.
  \item \textbf{Collection of observation outputs.} Finally collect, at each owner's output, its retained observation, private
policy record, and public tuple. The full boundaries can be taken as
\[
 A_{\mathrm{ann}}=\bigotimes_iD(\Omega_i),\qquad
 B_{\mathrm{ann}}=
   \bigotimes_jD(\Omega_j\times\mathsf{AnnPol}_j\times\mathsf{Msg}).
\]
Every component is a decision generator, nonstrategic data wiring, or an
exhibited parameter reindexing, so the process lies in
$\mathbf{DecArena}_N(\mathcal C)$.
  \item \textbf{Causal execution.} Evaluating each response and collector
gives the displayed record. The reporting components are tensored; the
message collector is their explicit delivery barrier. Coherence and
scheduling independence follow from Theorem~\ref{thm:egt-causal-protocol}.
  \item \textbf{Observation and knowledge.} The original carrier $W$ remains an ordinary reference index: its tuple of
observations supplies the finite input, so no finite realization of $W$ is
required.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}


\begin{construction}[Policy witnesses over a public message state]
\label{con:egt-announcement-policy-witnesses}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Form the fibre of policy witnesses.} For $u\in\mathcal U$ retain the ordinary dependent family
\[
 K_u=F^{-1}(u).
\]
Its total carrier has the canonical bijection
\[
 \coprod_{u\in\mathcal U}K_u\cong\mathcal X,
 \qquad(u,x)\longmapsto x,
\]
whose inverse is $x\mapsto(F(x),x)$.
  \item \textbf{Realize a witness.} In the finite realization, let
$g_{\mathrm{ann}}:\mathsf{AnnPol}\to
 \mathcal C(A_{\mathrm{ann}},B_{\mathrm{ann}})$ be the process just
constructed. Associate to $x=(w,\pi)\in K_u$ the realized arrow
$g_{\mathrm{ann}}(\pi)$. This is a witness realization of
Construction~\ref{con:egt-general-witness-family}; its dependent linear
transpose exists by the ordinary--linear adjunction.
  \item \textbf{Recover the policy record.} The family retains
every implementing policy and its private records, while $F$ gives the
exact logical comparison on retained message tests. Reconstructing its total
carrier recovers all of $\mathcal X$ and the attached realizations.
\end{enumerate}
\end{construction}

\subsection{Coalition ability through complete communication policies}

\begin{theorem}[Complete-policy announcement ability]
\label{thm:egt-complete-policy-announcement-ability}
For every goal $\Psi\hookrightarrow\mathcal U$ and coalition $C\subseteq N$,
\[
 \mathsf{AnnAbility}_C(\Psi)(w)
 \iff
 \exists\pi_C\in\prod_{i\in C}\mathsf{AnnPol}_i\;
 \forall\pi_{-C}\in\prod_{j\notin C}\mathsf{AnnPol}_j\;
       \Psi\bigl(F(w,(\pi_C,\pi_{-C}))\bigr).
\]
This is the paper's pointwise effectivity predicate, expressed through
the complete policy interfaces of the announcing agents.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=4pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \textbf{Ownerwise alternatives.} If $B_C$ is a winning legal coalition message at $w$, choose the explicit
policies $E_{i,B_i}$ for its members. Every outsider policy
evaluates to a legal outsider message, so every resulting joint message
satisfies $\Psi$.
  \item \textbf{Reverse implication.} Conversely, let $\pi_C$ satisfy the right-hand side and let
$B_C=(\pi_i(\bar o_i(w)))_{i\in C}$. Given any legal outsider tuple
$B_{-C}$, extend it by
$\pi_j=E_{j,B_j}$ for $j\notin C$. The resulting policy tuple
